94936.q: Where does deadly nightshade often grow?
a: In the middle of a lake
94936.e: Deadly nightshade likes to grow in bright spots in the forest, for example in clearings and along forest paths.
94936.m: Deadly nightshade can grow in forest clearings.

94937.q: What does the fruit of deadly nightshade look like?
94937.e: The fruit is a round berry the size of a cherry. That is why its German name means “mad cherry”.
94937.m: Deadly nightshade has berries that look like cherries.

94938.q: What happens to the eyes when someone has eaten deadly nightshade?
94938.e: The poison of deadly nightshade makes the pupils, the black dots in the eye, very wide. Everything then looks blurred.
94938.m: Huge pupils can be a sign of deadly nightshade poisoning.

94939.q: Which parts of deadly nightshade are poisonous?
94939.e: With deadly nightshade, all parts are poisonous, including the leaves, root and berries.
94939.m: No part of deadly nightshade is safe.

94940.q: What colour are the flowers of deadly nightshade?
94940.e: The bell-shaped flowers of deadly nightshade are brownish to purple. They hang singly on the plant.
94940.m: Deadly nightshade has brownish purple bell flowers.

94941.q: How tall can deadly nightshade grow?
a: Up to about as tall as a person
94941.e: Deadly nightshade is a large perennial plant. It usually grows 50 to 150 centimetres tall, sometimes even 2 metres.
94941.m: Deadly nightshade is a large plant.

94942.q: What colour are the flowers of monkshood?
94942.e: Monkshood has dark blue to purple flowers.

94943.q: What does the shape of the monkshood flower remind you of?
94943.e: The top petal arches over the flower like a helmet or a hood.
94943.m: The monkshood flower looks like a knight's helmet.

94944.e: Monkshood is thought to be the most poisonous plant in Europe. Even small amounts can be life-threatening.
94944.m: Always leave monkshood where it is.

94945.q: Why should you not even pick monkshood with bare hands?
a: The poison goes through the skin
94945.e: The poison of monkshood can work through the skin and make it burn and tingle. That is why you should not touch it.

94946.q: Where does monkshood often grow in Switzerland?
94946.e: Monkshood likes to grow in damp meadows and near alpine huts in the mountains. But you can also find it in gardens.
94946.m: When hiking in the mountains you may see monkshood.

94947.q: Which animals like to visit monkshood flowers?
94947.e: Bumblebees are strong enough to crawl into the helmet-shaped flower to get nectar. While doing so, they pollinate the flower.

94948.q: What should you do if a friend wants to pick monkshood flowers?
a: Warn them and fetch an adult
Pick some too and smell them
Put the flowers in your mouth
94948.e: Monkshood is very poisonous. You warn your friend and tell an adult.
94948.m: With poisonous plants, warn others and get help.

94949.q: Roughly how tall does monkshood grow?
a: Only as tall as a finger
Only as tall as a shoe
94949.e: Monkshood usually grows 50 to 150 centimetres tall. It often reaches a child's hip or higher.

94951.q: What colour are the flowers of the common foxglove usually?
94951.e: The flowers are usually purple-red to pink. Inside they have dark spots with a pale edge.
94951.m: The common foxglove has purple-red flowers.

94952.q: How are the flowers arranged on the stem of the foxglove?
a: One below the other on one side
As a single flower at the top
94952.e: Lots of flowers hang one below the other on one side of the tall stem, like bells on a pole.
94952.m: On the foxglove, lots of flowers hang on a long stem.

94953.q: Which organ does foxglove poison especially affect?
94953.e: Foxglove poison affects the heart. That is why all parts of the plant are dangerous.
94953.m: Foxglove is a poison for the heart.

95126.q: Which sense tells you whether something is rough or smooth?
95126.e: With the sense of touch you feel what a surface is like. You need neither eyes nor ears for it.
95126.m: With the sense of touch you feel rough and smooth.

95127.q: Where on the hand are there especially many touch receptors?
a: On the back of the hand
95127.e: There are a great many tiny sensors in the fingertips. That is why you can feel things especially finely with them.

95128.q: What do ants use to feel their way?
95128.e: Ants touch the ground and other ants with their movable antennae. They can also smell with them.

95129.q: Which part of its body does an elephant use to feel things especially finely?
95129.e: The tip of an elephant's trunk is very sensitive. With it, the elephant can even feel and grab small things like a peanut.
95129.m: An elephant feels things with its trunk.

95130.q: What do you say about someone who does a difficult thing very carefully and skilfully?
95130.e: Having a delicate touch means being sensitive and skilful. The phrase comes from the fine sense of touch in the fingers.
95130.m: Someone who is skilful and sensitive has a delicate touch.

95131.q: Where do the nerves report what the fingers feel?
95131.e: The nerves carry the messages from the skin to the brain in a flash. Only there do you notice what you are touching.
95131.m: The brain processes what the skin feels.

95132.q: What do babies very often use to feel objects?
95132.e: Lips and tongue can feel very finely. That is why babies put lots of things in their mouth to explore them.
95132.m: Babies often explore things with their mouth.

95133.q: What can you find out by touch with your eyes closed?
a: Whether something is soft or hard
95133.e: When you touch something, you feel whether it gives way or is firm. Colours and brightness, on the other hand, can only be seen.
95133.m: By touch you feel whether something is soft or hard.

95134.q: What do cats use to feel their surroundings in the dark?
95134.e: A cat's whiskers are very sensitive. They can feel even tiny movements of air and narrow gaps.

95135.q: What does a glowing sign on a switched-off hob mean?
95135.e: Even after it is switched off, a hob stays hot for a long time. The display warns you not to touch it.
95135.m: A heat warning light warns of a hot hob.

95136.q: What do you call a lightning-fast movement of the body that happens without thinking?
95136.e: In a reflex, the body reacts by itself and very quickly. This protects us from injuries.
95136.m: A reflex is a movement without thinking.

95137.q: What do you use to hold a hot pan?
95137.e: A thick oven glove only lets the heat through slowly. That way you do not burn your hands.
95137.m: You hold hot pans with an oven glove.

95138.q: What does the body do in great heat to cool down?
95138.e: Sweat comes out of the skin and evaporates. This makes the skin cooler.
95138.m: In the heat, the body cools down by sweating.

95139.q: Which part of the body do parents often use to check that a baby's bath water is not too hot?
95139.e: The skin on the elbow is thinner and less used to heat than the palm of the hand. So you can easily tell whether the water feels pleasant.
95139.m: You check the warmth of bath water with your elbow.

95140.q: What does your skin get if you stay in the sun too long without protection?
95140.e: The sun's rays damage the skin. It turns red, hot and painful. Sun cream and shade protect you.
95140.m: Too much sun gives you sunburn.

95141.q: What can form on the skin when you burn yourself?
95141.e: With a burn, fluid collects under the skin. This forms a blister, which you should not burst.
95141.m: A burn can cause a blister.

95142.q: Why should you not walk barefoot over hot tarmac in summer?
a: You can burn the soles of your feet
It makes you tired straight away
95142.e: Dark tarmac gets very hot in the sun. The skin on the soles of your feet can get burnt.
95142.m: Hot tarmac can burn the soles of your feet.

95143.q: What do you get on your skin when you are cold?
95143.e: In the cold, the tiny hairs stand up and the skin forms little bumps. In Switzerland people call this “chicken skin”.
95143.m: When you are cold, you get goose bumps.

95144.q: What does the body do to make heat when it is very cold?
95144.e: When you shiver, your muscles move very fast. This makes heat.
95144.m: Shivering warms the body in the cold.

95145.q: Which parts of the body usually get cold first?
95145.e: In the cold, the body sends warm blood mainly to the important organs. That is why fingers and toes get cold quickly.
95145.m: Fingers and toes get cold first.

95146.q: What is an injury to the skin caused by extreme cold called?
95146.e: In extreme cold, the skin on fingers, toes, ears or nose can be damaged. This is called frostbite.

95147.q: What protects your hands from the cold in winter?
95147.e: Gloves hold the warm air around your hands. That way your fingers do not cool down so quickly.
95147.m: Gloves keep your hands warm in winter.

95148.q: What happens to your hand if you hold an ice cube for a long time?
95148.e: The cold slows down the nerves in the skin. Then you feel almost nothing and your hand goes numb.
95148.m: Great cold makes the skin numb.

95149.q: What do you put on a fresh bump on the head?
95149.e: Cold makes the swelling less bad and eases the pain. Never put ice directly on the skin.

95150.q: Why does a metal railing feel colder in winter than a wooden one?
a: Wood is always in the sun
95150.e: Metal takes the warmth from your hand very quickly. That is why it feels colder, even when it is just as cold as the wood.
95150.m: Metal feels cold because it carries heat away quickly.

95151.q: Why is pain useful for the body?
95151.e: Pain is a warning signal. It shows that something is hurting the body or that something is wrong.

95152.q: What is a medicine that eases pain called?
95152.e: A painkiller dulls the pain. Children should only take it when an adult allows it.

95153.q: What does the number 0 mean on a pain scale from 0 to 10?
95153.e: With the pain scale you show the doctor how much something hurts. 0 means no pain, 10 the worst.
95153.m: On the pain scale, 0 means no pain.

95154.q: What is a blue mark that appears after a knock called?
95154.e: When you knock yourself, tiny blood vessels under the skin burst. The blood collects there and shows through blue.
95154.m: A blue mark is a bruise.

95155.q: What do you feel when you knock your funny bone on your elbow?
a: A warm tickle in your tummy
95155.e: At the elbow, a nerve lies right under the skin. If you hit it, it tingles all the way to your fingers.
95155.m: At the funny bone, a nerve lies right under the skin.

95157.q: What usually happens to the skin after a wasp sting?
95157.e: When a wasp stings, it injects a little poison into the skin. The spot turns red, swells and hurts.
95157.m: A wasp sting swells up and hurts.

95158.q: What should you do if a pain does not go away for a long time?
95158.e: Long or strong pain can be a sign of an illness. A doctor can find out where it comes from.
95158.m: With long-lasting pain you go to the doctor.

95159.q: Why can you not really tickle yourself?
a: The brain knows in advance where it will be touched
Your own fingers are too cold
95159.e: The brain plans your own movement and expects the touch. So the surprise is gone and it does not tickle.

95160.q: Where are many people especially ticklish?
a: On the soles of the feet
On the top of the head
95160.e: There are many sensitive nerves on the soles of the feet. A light touch there tickles many people a lot.
95160.m: Many people are ticklish on the soles of their feet.

95161.q: What do most people do when they are tickled?
95161.e: Tickling makes most people laugh. That happens even though it is not always pleasant.
95161.m: Most people laugh when they are tickled.

95162.q: Which animals make a laughing sound when tickled?
95162.e: Young chimpanzees and other great apes also pant when tickled, as if they were laughing. This is how they play together.

95163.q: What often makes you sneeze when your nose tickles?
95163.e: Dust irritates the lining of the nose. By sneezing, the body blasts it back out.
95163.m: Dust in the nose makes you sneeze.

95164.q: What should you do if someone says “Stop” while you are tickling them?
95164.e: Tickling can become unpleasant. Anyone who says stop must be taken seriously.
95164.m: If someone says stop, you stop.

95165.q: What do you feel when an ant crawls over your arm?
95165.e: Its little legs touch the fine hairs on the skin. You feel this as a light tingling or tickling.
95165.m: A crawling ant tingles on the skin.

95166.e: Blind people and people with very poor sight can read Braille. They do not need their eyes for it.

95167.q: What can you use to write Braille?
95167.e: A Braille writing machine presses the dots into thick paper from below. Today there are also printers for it.
95167.m: Braille is written with a Braille writing machine.

95168.q: How did Louis Braille become blind as a small child?
a: Through an accident in the workshop
Through a fall from a horse
95168.e: At about three years old, he hurt his eye with a sharp tool in his father's workshop. Later he went blind in both eyes.
95168.m: Louis Braille went blind through an accident.

95169.q: Where did Louis Braille hurt his eye as a small child?
95169.e: At about three years old, he was playing with a sharp tool in his father's workshop. He hurt his eye and later went completely blind.
95169.m: Louis Braille hurt himself in his father's workshop.

95170.q: Why are books in Braille much thicker than other books?
a: The dots take up a lot of space
The paper is made of wood
95170.e: The dots must be big enough to feel. That is why much less text fits on a page.
95170.m: Books in Braille are very thick.

95171.q: Roughly how old was Louis Braille when he invented his dot writing?
95171.e: Louis Braille finished his dot writing in 1825. He was only 16 years old at the time.
95171.m: Louis Braille was still a teenager when he invented the writing.

95172.q: Which writing for soldiers gave Louis Braille his idea?
a: A writing for reading in the dark
A writing made of smoke signals
95172.e: An army officer had invented a night writing made of raised dots. Braille turned it into a simpler writing.
95172.m: A night writing for soldiers gave Braille his idea.

95173.q: What do the signs of Braille feel like?
95173.e: The dots are pressed out of the paper. You feel them as little raised bumps.
95173.m: The dots of Braille stand out from the paper.

95174.q: What do you do on a barefoot trail?
95174.e: On a barefoot trail you take off your shoes and socks. With your bare feet you feel the ground.
95174.m: On a barefoot trail you walk without shoes.

95175.q: What do you feel with your feet on a barefoot trail?
95175.e: A barefoot trail goes over grass, sand, stones, bark or mud. Each surface feels different.
95175.m: On a barefoot trail you feel different surfaces.

95176.q: Which surface feels especially soft on a barefoot trail?
95176.e: Moss is a soft, damp cushion of tiny plants. Walking on it feels like walking on a carpet.
95176.m: Moss feels soft under your feet.

95177.q: Which surface prickles most under your feet?
95177.e: Fir cones are hard and spiky. Walking on them prickles the soles of your feet.
95177.m: Fir cones prickle under your feet.

95178.q: What should you do after a barefoot trail?
95178.e: After a barefoot trail your feet are often dirty. That is why many barefoot trails have a basin for washing at the end.
95178.m: After a barefoot trail you wash your feet.

95179.q: What gets especially strong when you walk barefoot?
95179.e: Without shoes, the small muscles in the foot work harder. That keeps the feet strong and flexible.
95179.m: Walking barefoot strengthens the foot muscles.

95180.q: In which canton is the well-known barefoot trail from Jakobsbad to Gontenbad?
95180.e: The barefoot trail runs through the hilly countryside near Gonten in the Appenzell region. It is a few kilometres long.
95180.m: A well-known barefoot trail is in the Appenzell region.

95181.q: Why is the grass often wet early in the morning?
95181.e: In the cool night, tiny drops of water from the air form on the grass. This is the dew.
95181.m: In the morning the grass is wet with dew.

95182.q: In which season do people most like going on a barefoot trail?
95182.e: In summer the ground is warm and pleasant. In winter and cool times it would be too cold for bare feet.
95182.m: Barefoot trails are best in summer.

95183.q: What do you do with a feely box?
95183.e: You reach into the box through a hole. You have to guess what is inside only by touch.
95183.m: In a feely box you recognise things by touch.

95184.q: Which parts of the body do you use most with a feely box?
95184.e: The objects are hidden so you cannot see them. You only recognise them by grabbing and feeling them.
95184.m: With a feely box you recognise things with your hands.

95185.q: What does a fir cone feel like in the feely box?
95185.e: A fir cone has lots of hard, scale-like parts. You can feel the edges well with your fingers.
95185.m: A fir cone feels rough and scaly.

95186.q: Which object feels soft and fluffy?
95186.e: Cotton wool is made of many fine fibres with air in between. That is why it is soft and fluffy.
95186.m: Cotton wool feels soft and fluffy.

95187.q: Which object feels smooth and cool?
95187.e: A metal spoon has no grooves and no fibres. It feels smooth and cool.
95187.m: A metal spoon feels smooth and cool.

95188.q: How do you recognise a walnut in the feely box?
a: It is hard with a wrinkly shell
95188.e: The shell of a walnut is hard and has lots of grooves. You can feel that well with your fingers.
95188.m: A walnut has a hard, wrinkly shell.

95189.q: Which object is soft, has lots of holes and soaks up water?
95189.e: A sponge is full of tiny holes. You can squeeze it and it takes in water.
95189.m: A sponge is soft and full of holes.

95190.q: Why should nothing sharp go into a feely box?
a: So that the box is lighter
So that you can see more
95190.e: You reach into the box without looking. Pointed or sharp things could hurt your hands.
95190.m: Nothing sharp goes into a feely box.

95191.q: What do you do almost automatically when something itches?
95191.e: An itch makes you want to scratch. Scratching helps for a moment, but it can irritate the skin.
95191.m: When something itches, you want to scratch.

95192.q: What itches for many people in spring when pollen is in the air?
95192.e: With hay fever, the body reacts to pollen. Then your eyes and nose itch and you have to sneeze.
95192.m: With hay fever, pollen makes your eyes and nose itch.

95193.q: Which plant stings and itches on the skin when you touch it?
95193.e: The stinging nettle has fine stinging hairs. When you touch them, they break off and release a burning juice into the skin. Small red bumps then appear that itch.
95193.m: The stinging nettle stings and itches on the skin.

95194.q: What often itches when a graze is healing?
95194.e: New skin grows under the scab. This often itches, but you should not pick off the scab.

95195.q: What can happen if you scratch a mosquito bite until it bleeds?
95195.e: Scratching gets dirt and germs into the little wound. Then it can get infected.

95196.q: Which small creatures can make your head itch and turn up in school classes?
95196.e: Head lice live in the hair. Their bites itch, and they do not jump but crawl from head to head.
95196.m: Head lice make your head itch.

95197.q: Which childhood illness causes lots of itchy blisters all over the body?
95197.e: With chickenpox, lots of small, itchy blisters appear on the skin. In Switzerland it is also called “Wilde Blattern”.

95198.q: What helps against dry, itchy skin in winter?
95198.e: A good cream keeps the skin moist and soft. Then it itches less.
95198.m: Putting cream on helps against dry skin.

95199.q: What do you feel when a shoe is too small?
95199.e: If a shoe is too small, it presses on your toes and foot. You feel this as unpleasant pressure.
95199.m: A shoe that is too small pinches.

95200.q: How do you check with your thumb whether a bicycle tyre has enough air?
95200.e: A well-pumped tyre hardly gives when you press it. If it is soft, it needs more air.
95200.m: By pressing, you check whether a tyre has enough air.

95201.q: What do you feel in your ears when you dive deep in the swimming pool?
95201.e: The deeper you dive, the more water presses down from above. You feel this especially in your ears.
95201.m: When diving, you feel pressure in your ears.

95202.q: What does a sock top that is too tight leave on your skin?
95202.e: The elastic presses into the skin for a long time. Afterwards you see red lines that soon disappear.
95202.m: Tight socks leave marks on the skin.

95203.q: What does the doctor measure with an inflatable cuff on the upper arm?
95203.e: The cuff squeezes the arm for a moment. A device measures how strongly the blood presses against the blood vessels.
95203.m: The cuff is used to measure blood pressure.

95204.q: Why does a pointed stone under your foot hurt more than a flat one?
a: Your weight presses on a small spot
95204.e: With a pointed stone, your whole weight presses on a tiny point. That is why the pressure there is very great.
95204.m: On a small area the pressure is especially great.

95205.q: What do you do with a clean cloth when a wound is bleeding heavily?
a: Press it firmly on the wound
Put it next to the wound
95205.e: Pressure on the wound slows the bleeding. Then you quickly get help.
95205.m: You press a clean cloth on a bleeding wound.

95206.q: What do you feel when the phone buzzes in your trouser pocket?
95206.e: Inside the phone, a tiny motor spins very fast. The device shakes and you feel it on your skin.

95207.q: What vibrates in your throat when you hum?
95207.e: When you hum, the vocal cords in the voice box vibrate. If you put your hand on your throat, you can feel the trembling.
95207.m: When you hum, your vocal cords vibrate.

95208.q: What do you feel under your feet when a heavy lorry drives past close by?
95208.e: The heavy lorry makes the ground vibrate. You feel this vibration with your feet.
95208.m: Heavy vehicles make the ground vibrate.

95209.q: What is a device that measures the shaking of earthquakes called?
95209.e: A seismograph records even the smallest movements of the ground. In Switzerland, the Swiss Seismological Service at ETH Zurich does the measuring.

95210.q: How can deaf people feel music?
95210.e: Loud music makes the floor and the air vibrate. Deaf people feel the bass with their whole body.
95210.m: Deaf people feel music through vibrations.

95211.q: What do you feel in your fingers when you pluck a guitar string?
95211.e: The plucked string swings back and forth. This makes the note, and you feel the fine trembling.

95212.q: How does a spider notice that an insect is caught in its web?
95212.e: The trapped insect wriggles and makes the threads vibrate. The spider feels this with its legs.
95212.m: A spider feels prey by the trembling of its web.

95213.q: What do you feel in your hand with an electric toothbrush?
95213.e: In an electric toothbrush, a motor moves the brush head very fast. You feel this as a vibration in your hand.

95214.q: What do people often put in bed in winter to make it warm?
95214.e: A hot-water bottle is filled with warm water. It warms the bed and your feet.
95214.m: A hot-water bottle warms the bed.

95215.q: Which material keeps you especially warm in winter?
95215.e: There is a lot of air trapped between the wool fibres. This air holds on to your body heat.
95215.m: Wool keeps you warm in winter.

95216.q: Which T-shirt gets warmer in the sun?
95216.e: Dark colours absorb more sunlight than light ones. That is why dark clothes get warmer in the sun.
95216.m: Dark clothes get warmer in the sun.

95217.q: Why do you rub your hands together when it is cold?
95217.e: When you rub things against each other, heat is produced. This is called friction heat.

95218.q: Why do emperor penguins stand close together in winter?
95218.e: In Antarctica it is freezing cold. Huddled close together, the penguins lose less heat.

95219.q: What do you feel on your skin when you sit close to a campfire?
95219.e: The fire sends out heat rays. They warm the skin even without you touching the fire.
95219.m: A campfire warms you with heat rays.

95220.q: Why does lukewarm water feel hot on your hands after a snowball fight?
a: Because your hands are very cold
95220.e: The skin compares the temperature with its own. So cold hands feel lukewarm water as hot.
95220.m: Cold hands feel lukewarm water as hot.

95221.q: Which stove heats the living room in many old Swiss farmhouses?
95221.e: A tiled stove stores the heat of the fire in its tiles. It gives it off to the room for a long time.
95221.m: A tiled stove keeps the room warm for a long time.

95222.q: Which colour on a tap usually shows warm water?
95222.e: Red stands for warm and blue for cold. That way you know which way to turn.
95222.m: On a tap, red means warm water.

95223.q: What tickles especially when you stroke it very lightly over the skin?
95223.e: A feather touches the skin only very gently. Many people feel this light touch as tickling.
95223.m: A feather tickles on the skin.

95224.q: What does a dog do with its mouth open to cool down in the heat?
95224.e: When panting, water evaporates from the tongue and mouth. This cools the dog down.

95225.q: What is the capital of the canton of Aargau?
95225.e: Aarau is the capital of the canton of Aargau. The government and the cantonal parliament work there.

95226.q: Which river gives the canton of Aargau its name?
95226.e: The name Aargau roughly means “land on the Aare”. The Aare flows right across the whole canton.
95226.m: Aargau means land on the Aare.

95227.q: Which neighbouring country borders the canton of Aargau to the north?
95227.e: In the north, the Rhine forms the border between Aargau and Germany.
95227.m: Across the Rhine, Aargau looks towards Germany.

95228.q: Which lake is in the canton of Aargau?
95228.e: Lake Hallwil lies in the Seetal valley in the canton of Aargau. In summer you can swim and take boat trips there.
95228.m: Lake Hallwil is the largest lake in Aargau.

95229.q: Which vegetable is in the famous cake from the canton of Aargau?
95229.e: Aargau carrot cake is baked with grated carrots and almonds. It is moist and often decorated with little marzipan carrots.
95229.m: Aargau carrot cake: carrots in the cake.

95230.q: Which language is mainly spoken in the canton of Aargau?
95230.e: In the canton of Aargau, German is the official language. In everyday life people speak the Aargau dialect, in other words Swiss German.

95231.q: What is the town of Baden in the canton of Aargau known for?
a: For warm spring water to bathe in
95231.e: In Baden, warm water comes out of the ground. Even the Romans bathed there, which is why the town is called Baden, German for “bathing”.
95231.m: In Baden people bathe in warm spring water.

95232.q: How many white stars are on the coat of arms of the canton of Aargau?
95232.e: The Aargau coat of arms is divided into two halves. On the left is a white river on black, on the right three white stars on blue.
95232.m: Three stars on blue: that is Aargau.

95233.q: Which three rivers meet at the “water castle of Switzerland” in the canton of Aargau?
95233.e: Near Brugg and Windisch, the Reuss and the Limmat flow into the Aare. Because so much water comes together here, the area is called the “water castle of Switzerland”.
95233.m: The Aare, Reuss and Limmat meet at the water castle.

95234.q: What nickname does the canton of Aargau have?
95234.e: Aargau is often called the “canton of culture”. It has many castles, palaces, monasteries and museums.
95234.m: Aargau is the canton of culture.

95235.q: What is the big town festival called that is celebrated in Baden in the canton of Aargau about every ten years?
95235.e: The Badenfahrt is a huge public festival with a parade, food stalls and music. It only takes place about every ten years.
95235.m: Every ten years Baden celebrates the Badenfahrt.

95236.q: What is produced at the Riburg saltworks near Möhlin in the canton of Aargau?
95236.e: There is salt deep underground. At the Riburg saltworks it is dissolved in water, pumped up and then made into table salt and road salt.
95236.m: At Riburg, salt is brought up from deep underground.

95237.q: Which famous moated castle stands on Lake Hallwil in the canton of Aargau?
95237.e: Hallwyl Castle stands on two small islands and is surrounded by water. Today it is a museum.
95237.m: Hallwyl Castle stands in the middle of the water.

95238.q: Roughly how many people live in the canton of Aargau?
95238.e: More than 700,000 people live in Aargau. That makes it one of the most populous cantons in Switzerland.

95239.q: Which of these cantons is a neighbour of the canton of Aargau?
95239.e: Aargau borders Zurich, Zug, Lucerne, Bern, Solothurn and Basel-Landschaft. Thurgau, Glarus and Schwyz do not touch Aargau.

95240.q: What nickname does the old town of Aarau have because of its painted eaves?
95240.e: Many houses in Aarau's old town have brightly painted undersides to their roofs. That is why Aarau is called the “town of beautiful gables”.
95240.m: Aarau is the town of beautiful gables.

95246.q: Which well-known mountain is on the border of the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden?
95246.e: At 2,502 metres, the Säntis is the highest mountain in the Alpstein. On its summit, Appenzell Innerrhoden, Appenzell Ausserrhoden and St Gallen meet.
95246.m: The Säntis is the king of the Alpstein.

95247.q: Which mountain lake lies below the Ebenalp in the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden?
95247.e: The Seealpsee lies in the Alpstein. You can reach it on foot from Wasserauen.
95247.m: The Seealpsee sparkles in the Alpstein.

95248.q: Which animal is on the coat of arms of the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden?
95248.e: The coat of arms of Appenzell Innerrhoden shows an upright black bear on a white background.
95248.m: A black bear decorates the Innerrhoden coat of arms.

95249.q: Which language is spoken in the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden?
95249.e: In Appenzell Innerrhoden people speak German. In everyday life you hear the typical Appenzell dialect.
95249.m: Innerrhoden speaks German with an Appenzell dialect.

95250.q: Which sweet pastry with an almond filling is a speciality from Appenzell?
95250.e: The Appenzeller Biber is a gingerbread with an almond filling. Often a picture is pressed into the dough.
95250.m: A Biber from Appenzell is gingerbread with an almond filling.

95251.q: How do people vote at the Landsgemeinde in Appenzell Innerrhoden?
95251.e: At the Landsgemeinde, the voters gather in the open air. They vote by raising their hands.
95251.m: At the Landsgemeinde, the raised hand counts.

95252.q: Which musical instrument, whose strings are struck with small hammers, belongs to Appenzell folk music?
95252.e: The hammered dulcimer (Hackbrett) is a box with many strings that you strike with two small hammers. It is part of typical Appenzell string music.
95252.m: The hammered dulcimer is heard in every Appenzell string band.

95253.q: In which part of Switzerland is the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden?
95253.e: Appenzell Innerrhoden is in eastern Switzerland, not far from Lake Constance. Together with Ausserrhoden it is surrounded by the canton of St Gallen.

95254.q: Which canton is even smaller in area than Appenzell Innerrhoden?
95254.e: Appenzell Innerrhoden is the second-smallest canton in Switzerland. Only Basel-Stadt has an even smaller area.
95254.m: Only Basel-Stadt is smaller than Innerrhoden.

95255.q: What is the famous mountain inn called that clings to a rock face below the Ebenalp in Appenzell Innerrhoden?
95255.e: The Aescher mountain inn is built right against a steep rock face. Photos of it are famous all over the world.
95255.m: The Aescher clings to the rock below the Ebenalp.

95256.q: On which mountain in Appenzell Innerrhoden is there a revolving restaurant with a view into the Rhine Valley?
95256.e: On the Hoher Kasten, the restaurant slowly turns in a circle. So you can see into the Rhine Valley, over Lake Constance and to the mountains.
95256.m: On the Hoher Kasten the restaurant turns round.

95257.q: On which day does the Landsgemeinde in Appenzell Innerrhoden normally take place?
a: On the last Sunday in April
On the first Monday in January
95257.e: The Innerrhoden Landsgemeinde takes place every year on the last Sunday in April on the Landsgemeinde square in Appenzell.
95257.m: Last Sunday in April: Landsgemeinde in Appenzell.

95258.q: What is the mountain range in Appenzell Innerrhoden called that the Säntis and Hoher Kasten belong to?
95258.e: The Alpstein is a small, rocky mountain range in eastern Switzerland. The Säntis, the Hoher Kasten and the Ebenalp belong to it.
95258.m: The Säntis and Hoher Kasten belong to the Alpstein.

95259.q: Which state was the last of the 13 old members to join the Swiss Confederacy?
95259.e: Appenzell joined in 1513 as the 13th and last member. At that time it was still a single state; the split into Inner and Outer Rhoden came later.
95259.m: Appenzell was the 13th member of the old Confederacy.

95260.q: Which two cantons does the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden border?
95260.e: Appenzell Innerrhoden only borders Appenzell Ausserrhoden and St Gallen. It does not border another country.
95260.m: Innerrhoden's neighbours are Ausserrhoden and St Gallen.

95261.q: How do you travel from Wasserauen up to the Ebenalp in Appenzell Innerrhoden?
95261.e: The Ebenalp railway is a cable car. It starts in Wasserauen, where the Appenzell Railway also ends, and glides up in a few minutes.
95261.m: You glide up to the Ebenalp by cable car.

95268.q: Which municipality is the largest in the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden?
95268.e: Herisau is the largest municipality in Appenzell Ausserrhoden. The government and the cantonal parliament also have their seat here.
95268.m: Herisau is the largest place in Ausserrhoden.

95269.q: Which custom takes place on New Year's Eve in Appenzell Ausserrhoden, for example in Urnäsch?
95269.e: At Silvesterchlausen, dressed-up figures called Chläuse go from house to house with big bells. They sing a yodel-like song called a Zäuerli and wish everyone a happy new year.
95269.m: On New Year's Eve the Chläuse go round in Urnäsch.

95270.q: What do the Silvesterchläuse in Appenzell Ausserrhoden wear so they can be heard from far away?
95270.e: The Chläuse wear heavy bells. When they move, these ring loudly.

95271.q: Which dog breed bears the name of the Appenzell region?
95271.e: The Appenzeller Sennenhund is a herding dog from the Appenzell region. It has black, white and brown markings and is very lively.
95271.m: The Appenzeller Sennenhund herds the cows.

95272.q: Which canton surrounds Appenzell Ausserrhoden on almost all sides?
95272.e: Appenzell Ausserrhoden lies in the middle of the canton of St Gallen. Apart from St Gallen it only borders Appenzell Innerrhoden.
95272.m: Ausserrhoden lies in the middle of the canton of St Gallen.

95273.q: Which language is spoken in the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden?
95273.e: In Appenzell Ausserrhoden people speak German. In everyday life you hear the Appenzell dialect.

95274.q: Which big lake can you see from the village of Heiden in Appenzell Ausserrhoden?
95274.e: Heiden lies high above Lake Constance. From there you have a wide view across the lake to Germany and Austria.
95274.m: From Heiden you look out over Lake Constance.

95275.e: Mostbröckli is beef that is seasoned, smoked and dried. It is eaten in thin slices, for example as a mid-morning snack.
95275.m: Mostbröckli is smoked beef from the Appenzell region.

95276.q: Which two letters are next to the bear on the coat of arms of Appenzell Ausserrhoden?
95276.e: The letters V and R stand for “Usser Rhoden”, meaning the outer Rhoden. This is how the coat of arms differs from that of Innerrhoden.
95276.m: V and R mean Usser Rhoden.

95277.q: Which well-known children's village is in Trogen in the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden?
95277.e: The Pestalozzi Children's Village was founded in Trogen in 1946 to give children a home after the Second World War. Today the foundation works for education and understanding.
95277.m: The Pestalozzi Children's Village is in Trogen.

95278.q: Which founder of the Red Cross spent the last years of his life in Heiden in Appenzell Ausserrhoden?
95278.e: Henry Dunant lived in Heiden from 1887 and died there in 1910. The Henry Dunant Museum in Heiden tells his story.
95278.m: Henry Dunant spent his last years in Heiden.

95279.q: From which place in Appenzell Ausserrhoden does the cable car go up the Säntis?
95279.e: The Säntis cable car starts at the Schwägalp. In a few minutes it takes visitors up to the summit.
95279.m: From the Schwägalp you glide up the Säntis.

95280.q: Which three kinds of Silvesterchläuse are there in Appenzell Ausserrhoden?
95280.e: The Schöne (the beautiful ones) wear splendid headdresses, the Wüeschte (the ugly ones) are made of fir branches, moss and leaves. The Schö-Wüeschte are a mixture of both.

95281.q: Roughly how many people live in the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden?
95281.e: About 55,000 people live in Appenzell Ausserrhoden. That is clearly more than in Innerrhoden, but far fewer than in big cantons.

95282.q: What is the typical painting style from the Appenzell region called that shows cows and herdsmen moving up to the alpine pastures?
95282.e: Appenzell peasant painting, also called herdsmen's painting, shows herdsmen, cows and goats on the way up to the alpine pasture. The pictures often decorate furniture and the bases of milking buckets.
95282.m: Peasant painting shows the procession to the alpine pastures.

95283.q: How can you recognise a typical Appenzell farmhouse in Appenzell Ausserrhoden?
a: By wooden shingles and long rows of windows
By a flat roof with a garden
By walls of clay and straw
95283.e: Appenzell houses are built of wood and often covered with shingles. Typical are the many windows side by side on the gable end.
95283.m: Many windows in a row: that is an Appenzell house.

95290.q: Which important building in Swiss politics stands in the city of Bern?
95290.e: In the Federal Palace in Bern, the Federal Council and the Swiss parliament work. It has a large green dome.
95290.m: Switzerland is governed from the Federal Palace in Bern.

95291.q: What is the famous tower with an astronomical clock in Bern's old town called?
95291.e: The Zytglogge is an old tower with an astronomical clock. Shortly before every full hour, funny figures move.
95291.m: At the Zytglogge in Bern, the figures dance on the hour.

95292.q: Which river flows in a big loop around Bern's old town?
95292.e: The Aare flows almost all the way round Bern's old town. In summer many people swim in the river.
95292.m: The Aare hugs Bern's old town.

95293.q: Which town in the canton of Bern lies between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz?
95293.e: Interlaken means “between the lakes”. The town lies exactly between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz.

95294.q: Which three famous mountains stand side by side in the Bernese Oberland?
95294.e: The Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau stand side by side in the Bernese Oberland. You can see them well, for example, from Grindelwald or Interlaken.
95294.m: The Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau are Bern's famous trio.

95295.q: Which famous cheese with big holes comes from the canton of Bern?
95295.e: Emmental cheese comes from the Emmental valley in the canton of Bern. It is known for its big, round holes.
95295.m: Holes in the cheese? That is Emmental.

95296.q: Which two languages are official languages in the canton of Bern?
95296.e: In the canton of Bern, German and French are official languages. In the Bernese Jura people mainly speak French.

95297.q: Where in the city of Bern can you watch real bears by the Aare?
95297.e: In the Bear Park on the banks of the Aare, bears live in a large enclosure. It is right next to the old bear pit.
95297.m: Real bears live in Bern's Bear Park.

95298.q: What is Bern's old town part of?
a: The Seven Wonders of the World
95298.e: Bern's old town became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983. It is especially well preserved and has long arcades and many fountains.
95298.m: Bern's old town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

95299.q: What are the covered walkways along the houses in Bern's old town called?
95299.e: There are kilometres of arcades (Lauben) in Bern's old town. Under these archways you can shop and stay dry even when it rains.
95299.m: In Bern you stroll dry under the arcades.

95300.q: What is the market in Bern called where mainly onions are sold on the fourth Monday in November?
95300.e: At the Zibelemärit (onion market), farmers sell onions, often woven into artistic plaits. There is also confetti and onion tart.
95300.m: At the Zibelemärit, everything is about onions.

95301.q: Which station on the border between the cantons of Bern and Valais is the highest railway station in Europe?
95301.e: The Jungfraujoch is 3,454 metres above sea level. The Jungfrau Railway goes there through a tunnel in the Eiger and Mönch.
95301.m: The Jungfraujoch is the highest railway station in Europe.

95302.q: Which town in the canton of Bern is the largest bilingual town in Switzerland?
95302.e: In Biel/Bienne many people speak German and many speak French. Street signs there are in both languages.

95303.q: Which waterfall near Meiringen in the canton of Bern is known from the Sherlock Holmes stories?
95303.e: The writer Arthur Conan Doyle made the Reichenbach Falls the setting of a famous Sherlock Holmes story. There is even a Sherlock Holmes Museum in Meiringen.
95303.m: Sherlock Holmes and the Reichenbach Falls belong together.

95304.q: Which triangular chocolate was invented in Bern in 1908?
95304.e: Theodor Tobler and Emil Baumann invented Toblerone in Bern in 1908. The triangular shape reminds many people of mountain peaks.

95305.q: Which valley in the Bernese Oberland is known for its many waterfalls, for example the Staubbach Falls?
95305.e: In the Lauterbrunnen Valley, more than 70 waterfalls plunge down from high rock faces. The Staubbach Falls are one of the best known.
95305.m: Many waterfalls rush down in the Lauterbrunnen Valley.

95312.q: Which neighbouring country does the canton of Basel-Landschaft border along the Rhine?
95312.e: Germany is on the other side of the Rhine. So the Rhine is part of the border between Basel-Landschaft and Germany.
95312.m: Across the Rhine, the Baselbiet looks towards Germany.

95313.q: What colour is the Basel staff on the coat of arms of the canton of Basel-Landschaft?
95313.e: The coat of arms of Basel-Landschaft shows a red Basel staff with small spikes on a white background. The Basel staff of Basel-Stadt, by contrast, is black.

95314.q: Which fruit is the canton of Basel-Landschaft especially known for?
95314.e: A great many cherry trees grow in the Baselbiet. In spring they blossom white, and in summer the cherries are picked.

95315.q: What do many people call the canton of Basel-Landschaft in everyday life?
95315.e: Instead of Basel-Landschaft, people often simply say “Baselbiet”. The people there are called Baselbieter.
95315.m: In everyday life, Basel-Landschaft is called the Baselbiet.

95316.q: Which language is spoken in the canton of Basel-Landschaft?
95316.e: In the canton of Basel-Landschaft, German is the official language. In everyday life people speak the Baselbiet dialect.
95316.m: In the Baselbiet people speak German.

95317.q: Which small neighbouring canton containing the city of Basel borders Basel-Landschaft?
95317.e: Basel-Stadt and Basel-Landschaft used to be a single canton. Today they are two cantons right next to each other.

95318.q: Which big river flows past the canton of Basel-Landschaft in the north?
95318.e: The Rhine flows past places such as Augst, Pratteln and Birsfelden. Big ships sail on it all the way to the sea.
95318.m: The Rhine flows past the Baselbiet.

95319.q: What is the famous old town gate of Liestal in the canton of Basel-Landschaft called?
95319.e: The Törli is the landmark of Liestal. You enter the old town through this old town gate.
95319.m: The Törli is the gate to Liestal's old town.

95320.q: What is the fire custom at carnival in Liestal called, in which burning carts are pulled through the town?
95320.e: At Chienbäse, people carry burning bundles of pinewood and pull fire carts through the Törli. The spectacle takes place on the evening of carnival Sunday.
95320.m: At Chienbäse, Liestal is ablaze at carnival.

95321.q: Which of these cantons is a neighbour of Basel-Landschaft?
95321.e: Basel-Landschaft borders Basel-Stadt, Aargau, Solothurn and Jura. Lucerne, Zurich and Neuchâtel are further away.
95321.m: Jura is a neighbour of the Baselbiet.

95322.q: Which river flows through the Laufen valley in the canton of Basel-Landschaft and joins the Rhine at Basel?
95322.e: The Birs comes from the Jura, flows through the Laufen valley and joins the Rhine at Birsfelden and Basel.
95322.m: The Birs flows through the Laufen valley to the Rhine.

95323.q: Which river flows through Liestal and joins the Rhine at Augst?
95323.e: The Ergolz flows through the Ergolz valley and through Liestal. At Augst, where the Roman town is, it flows into the Rhine.
95323.m: The Ergolz flows through Liestal to Augst.

95324.q: In which municipality in the canton of Basel-Landschaft is there a baroque cathedral?
95324.e: Arlesheim Cathedral was built in the 17th century and later remodelled in baroque style. Nearby is the Ermitage, a beautiful landscape garden.

95325.q: Roughly how many people live in the canton of Basel-Landschaft?
95325.e: Just under 300,000 people live in the canton of Basel-Landschaft. That is more than in Basel-Stadt.
95325.m: The Baselbiet has just under 300,000 inhabitants.

95326.q: Which mountain range with gentle hills and limestone cliffs shapes the canton of Basel-Landschaft?
95326.e: A large part of the Baselbiet lies in the Jura. Typical features are table mountains, limestone cliffs and valleys with many cherry trees.
95326.m: The Baselbiet lies in the Jura.

95327.q: Which neighbouring country does the canton of Basel-Landschaft border in the Leimental?
95327.e: In the Leimental, for example near Schönenbuch, Basel-Landschaft borders France. On the Rhine the canton borders Germany.
95327.m: In the Leimental, France is right next door.

95334.q: What is the capital of the canton of Basel-Stadt?
95334.e: The city of Basel is the capital of the canton of Basel-Stadt. Liestal is the capital of the neighbouring canton of Basel-Landschaft.
95334.m: In the canton of Basel-Stadt, Basel is the capital.

95335.q: Which big river flows right through the city of Basel in the canton of Basel-Stadt?
95335.e: The Rhine divides Basel into two parts. In summer many people swim in the Rhine.

95336.q: Which two countries does the canton of Basel-Stadt border?
95336.e: Basel is right in the north of Switzerland. From there it is only a short way to Germany and to France.

95337.q: What do the people of the canton of Basel-Stadt affectionately call their zoo?
95337.e: Basel Zoo is called the “Zolli”. It is the oldest zoo in Switzerland.

95338.q: What can be seen on the coat of arms of the canton of Basel-Stadt?
a: A black Basel staff on a white background
A black bear on a yellow background
A white cross on a red background
A black bull on a yellow background
95338.e: The Basel coat of arms shows the Basel staff. It looks like a bishop's crook.
95338.m: The black Basel staff is the symbol of Basel-Stadt.

95339.q: Which spicy biscuit with honey is a well-known speciality from the canton of Basel-Stadt?
95339.e: Basler Läckerli are small, hard gingerbread biscuits with honey, spices, almonds and candied orange peel. You can buy them all year round.

95340.q: What is the canton of Basel-Stadt compared with all the other cantons of Switzerland?
95340.e: Basel-Stadt is only about 37 square kilometres in size. No other canton has a smaller area.
95340.m: Basel-Stadt is the smallest canton in Switzerland.

95341.q: How do the small ferries cross the Rhine in the city of Basel in the canton of Basel-Stadt?
a: Using the force of the Rhine's current
95341.e: The Basel Rhine ferries hang from a cable across the river. The current of the water pushes them to the other bank, without any engine at all.
95341.m: The Basel ferries are powered by the Rhine.

95342.q: How many municipalities are there in the canton of Basel-Stadt?
95342.e: The canton is made up of the city of Basel and the municipalities of Riehen and Bettingen. So it has only three municipalities.
95342.m: Basel, Riehen and Bettingen make up the canton of Basel-Stadt.

95343.q: Which stone is Basel Minster in the canton of Basel-Stadt mainly built from?
95343.e: Basel Minster glows reddish because it is built of red sandstone. It stands high above the Rhine.
95343.m: Basel Minster is made of red sandstone.

95344.q: What colour is the façade of the famous town hall on the market square in Basel in the canton of Basel-Stadt?
95344.e: Basel Town Hall is painted bright red and decorated with colourful pictures. The cantonal government and parliament meet here.

95345.q: What is the place in Basel's Rhine port in the canton of Basel-Stadt called where Switzerland, Germany and France meet?
95345.e: At the Dreiländereck (three-country corner), three countries meet. A monument at the Rhine port marks this special spot.
95345.m: At the Dreiländereck in Basel, three countries meet.

95346.q: As far as which sea can ships sail from the Rhine ports in the canton of Basel-Stadt?
95346.e: The Rhine flows through Germany and the Netherlands into the North Sea. That is why the Basel Rhine ports are Switzerland's gateway to the sea.
95346.m: From Basel the Rhine leads to the North Sea.

95347.q: Which industry is especially important for the economy of the canton of Basel-Stadt?
95347.e: Big pharmaceutical companies such as Roche and Novartis have their headquarters in Basel. They make medicines for the whole world.
95347.m: Basel is a city of the pharmaceutical industry.

95348.q: What is the famous old town gate in Basel in the canton of Basel-Stadt called?
95348.e: The Spalentor is one of the most beautiful town gates in Switzerland. It used to be part of Basel's town wall.
95348.m: The Spalentor is Basel's famous town gate.

95349.q: What is the waterproof swimming bag called that you pack your clothes in when swimming in the Rhine in the canton of Basel-Stadt?
95349.e: The Wickelfisch is a waterproof bag shaped like a fish. You pack your clothes in it and let yourself drift down the Rhine with it.
95349.m: When swimming in the Rhine in Basel, the Wickelfisch swims along.

95356.q: What is the capital of the canton of Fribourg?
95356.e: The city of Fribourg, Freiburg in German, is the capital of the canton. It has a beautiful medieval old town.
95356.m: Fribourg is the capital of the canton of Fribourg.

95357.q: Which famous cheese comes from the canton of Fribourg?
95357.e: Gruyère is named after the Gruyère region in the canton of Fribourg. It is eaten all over the world.
95357.m: Gruyère comes from the Gruyère region in the canton of Fribourg.

95358.q: What colours does the coat of arms of the canton of Fribourg have?
a: Black at the top, white at the bottom
Red at the top, yellow at the bottom
Blue at the top, white at the bottom
Green at the top, white at the bottom
95358.e: The Fribourg coat of arms is divided horizontally into two halves. The top half is black, the bottom half white.

95359.q: In which little town in the canton of Fribourg is there a well-known castle on a hill, after which a cheese is also named?
95359.e: The little town of Gruyères with its castle stands on a hill in the Gruyère region. It is visited by many tourists every year.

95360.q: Which lake lies next to the town of Murten in the canton of Fribourg?
95360.e: The town of Murten lies right on Lake Murten. In summer you can swim and take boat trips there.

95361.q: What is the crème double from the Gruyère region in the canton of Fribourg?
95361.e: “Crème double de la Gruyère” is a very thick cream. People love to eat it with meringues.
95361.m: Meringues with double cream are a Fribourg dessert.

95362.q: What does the Cailler factory in Broc in the canton of Fribourg make?
95362.e: Cailler is one of the oldest chocolate brands in Switzerland. In Broc you can visit the factory and taste chocolate.
95362.m: Cailler chocolate is made in Broc.

95363.q: Which large canton borders the canton of Fribourg to the east?
95363.e: The canton of Fribourg has two main neighbouring cantons: Bern to the east and Vaud to the west and south. It also borders Neuchâtel across Lake Neuchâtel.

95364.q: What goes into a “moitié moitié” fondue from the canton of Fribourg?
95364.e: “Moitié moitié” means “half and half” in French. For this fondue, two Fribourg cheeses are mixed.
95364.m: Moitié moitié means half Gruyère, half Vacherin.

95365.q: What is the traditional autumn festival in the canton of Fribourg called, with a big feast of many courses?
95365.e: The Bénichon, called Kilbi in German, is a thanksgiving festival for the harvest and the return of the cows from the alpine pastures. It includes a long menu with many specialities.
95365.m: In autumn Fribourg celebrates the Bénichon.

95366.q: Which river flows through the city of Fribourg in the canton of Fribourg?
95366.e: The Sarine, Saane in German, winds through a deep gorge around Fribourg's old town. Many bridges cross the river.

95367.q: What is the cathedral in the city of Fribourg in the canton of Fribourg called?
95367.e: St Nicholas Cathedral has a tower 74 metres high. From the top you can see over the whole old town.
95367.m: St Nicholas Cathedral is in Fribourg.

95368.q: What is special about the University of Fribourg in the canton of Fribourg?
a: You can study in German and in French
It is the only university in the mountains
It is the oldest university in the world
95368.e: The University of Fribourg is bilingual. Students can take their courses in German, in French or in both languages.
95368.m: The University of Fribourg is bilingual.

95369.q: What can you still walk along today in the old town of Murten in the canton of Fribourg?
95369.e: Murten has a well-preserved medieval town wall. You can walk along the wall walk and look out over the roofs.
95369.m: You can walk along Murten's town wall.

95370.q: What is a well-known viewpoint mountain in the Gruyère region in the canton of Fribourg called?
95370.e: The Moléson is about 2,000 metres high. By funicular and cable car you can get almost to the summit.
95370.m: The Moléson is the viewpoint mountain of the Gruyère region.

95371.q: Which large reservoir lies in the canton of Fribourg?
95371.e: Lake Gruyère, Lac de la Gruyère in French, was created by a dam on the Sarine. It provides water for electricity.
95371.m: Lake Gruyère is a reservoir on the Sarine.

95378.q: What is the huge water fountain in Lake Geneva in the canton of Geneva called?
95378.e: The Jet d'eau is the landmark of Geneva. It shoots water very high into the air.
95378.m: The Jet d'eau is the landmark of Geneva.

95379.q: Which language is spoken in the canton of Geneva?
95379.e: Geneva is in western Switzerland, the Romandie. People speak French there.

95380.q: Which lake is the city of Geneva in the canton of Geneva on?
95380.e: The city of Geneva lies at the south-western end of Lake Geneva. In French the lake is called Lac Léman.

95381.q: Which country borders the canton of Geneva on almost all sides?
95381.e: The canton of Geneva is almost entirely surrounded by France. Only in the north-east does it border the canton of Vaud.
95381.m: Geneva is almost entirely surrounded by France.

95382.q: What is the famous big clock in the English Garden in Geneva made of?
95382.e: The flower clock in the Jardin Anglais is planted with thousands of flowers. It is a reminder that many watches are made in Geneva.
95382.m: In Geneva there is a clock made of flowers.

95383.q: What can be seen on the coat of arms of the canton of Geneva?
a: Half an eagle and a key
95383.e: On the left is half a black eagle on a yellow background. On the right is a golden key on a red background.
95383.m: Geneva has an eagle and a key on its coat of arms.

95384.q: What is the canton of Geneva especially famous for all over the world?
95384.e: Watches have been made in Geneva for centuries. Many famous watch companies are based there.
95384.m: Geneva is a city of watches.

95385.q: Which river flows out of Lake Geneva in the city of Geneva in the canton of Geneva?
95385.e: The Rhône first flows into Lake Geneva and leaves it again in Geneva. Then it flows on through France to the Mediterranean.
95385.m: In Geneva the Rhône leaves Lake Geneva.

95386.q: Roughly how high does the Jet d'eau in the canton of Geneva shoot?
95386.e: The Jet d'eau shoots water about 140 metres high. That is higher than most church towers.
95386.m: The Jet d'eau is about 140 metres high.

95387.q: Which aid organisation was founded in Geneva in the canton of Geneva in 1863?
95387.e: In 1863 Henry Dunant and other Genevans founded the committee that became the International Committee of the Red Cross. It helps people in need.
95387.m: The Red Cross was founded in Geneva.

95388.q: Which big research centre for particle physics is in the canton of Geneva?
95388.e: At CERN, scientists research what the world is made of. There is a gigantic particle accelerator in an underground tunnel there.
95388.m: CERN carries out research near Geneva.

95389.q: Which river joins the Rhône in the city of Geneva in the canton of Geneva?
95389.e: The Arve comes from the French Alps. At the Jonction in Geneva it flows into the Rhône, and you can see the two different colours of water.
95389.m: In Geneva the Arve flows into the Rhône.

95390.q: What is the cathedral in Geneva's old town in the canton of Geneva called?
95390.e: St Pierre Cathedral stands on the highest point of Geneva's old town. From its towers there is a great view.
95390.m: St Pierre Cathedral is in Geneva.

95391.q: Which Genevan received the very first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901?
95391.e: Henry Dunant co-founded the Red Cross. For this he received the first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901.
95391.m: Henry Dunant received the first Nobel Peace Prize.

95392.q: What are the small yellow boats called that cross the lake like a bus in the canton of Geneva?
95392.e: The Mouettes, meaning seagulls, take people from one side of the lake to the other. They are part of Geneva's public transport.
95392.m: In Geneva the yellow Mouettes cross the lake.

95393.q: In which country is the Salève, the local mountain of the people in the canton of Geneva?
95393.e: The Salève is just across the border in France. Even so, the people of Geneva call it their local mountain.
95393.m: Geneva's local mountain, the Salève, is in France.

95400.q: What is the capital of the canton of Glarus?
95400.e: The capital has the same name as the canton: Glarus. The Landsgemeinde takes place there every year.
95400.m: The capital of Glarus is called Glarus.

95401.q: What is the beautiful mountain lake in the Klöntal valley in the canton of Glarus called?
95401.e: Lake Klöntal lies in a valley west of Glarus. The mountains are beautifully reflected in the water.
95401.m: Lake Klöntal is in the Klöntal valley.

95402.q: What colour is Glarner Schabziger, a cheese from the canton of Glarus?
95402.e: Schabziger is a small, cone-shaped cheese. It is green because a special herb is mixed into it.

95403.q: Which language is spoken in the canton of Glarus?
95403.e: In the canton of Glarus people speak German. In everyday life they speak the Glarus dialect.

95404.q: Which sweet pastry is a speciality from the canton of Glarus?
95404.e: The Glarner Pastete is made of puff pastry. It is filled with almond paste and plum purée.
95404.m: The Glarner Pastete is filled with almonds and plums.

95405.q: Which river flows through the valley of the canton of Glarus?
95405.e: The Linth rises in the south of the canton and flows through the whole Glarus region. Then it flows into Lake Walen.
95405.m: The Linth flows through the Glarus region.

95406.q: Which canton is a neighbour of the canton of Glarus?
95406.e: Glarus borders St Gallen, Schwyz, Uri and the Grisons. Geneva, Basel-Stadt and Ticino are far away.
95406.m: The Grisons is a neighbour of Glarus.

95407.q: Which lake does the canton of Glarus share with the canton of St Gallen?
95407.e: Lake Walen lies between high mountains. Part of its shore belongs to Glarus, the other part to St Gallen.
95407.m: Glarus and St Gallen share Lake Walen.

95408.q: What is the highest mountain in the canton of Glarus called?
95408.e: The Tödi is about 3,600 metres high. It lies on the border with the Grisons.
95408.m: The Tödi is the highest mountain in Glarus.

95409.q: How do you get to the car-free village of Braunwald in the canton of Glarus?
a: By car over a pass road
By rack railway through a tunnel
95409.e: Braunwald lies on a sunny terrace above Linthal. From Linthal the Braunwald railway, a funicular, goes up to the village.
95409.m: You take the funicular to Braunwald.

95410.q: How many municipalities has the canton of Glarus had since 2011?
95410.e: In 2011 the many small municipalities were merged into three big ones. They are called Glarus Nord, Glarus and Glarus Süd.

95411.q: Which pass links the canton of Glarus with the canton of Uri?
95411.e: The road over the Klausen Pass leads from Linthal to Altdorf. In winter the pass is closed.
95411.m: The Klausen Pass links Glarus and Uri.

95412.q: What colour is Schabziger, a cheese from the canton of Glarus?
95412.e: Schabziger contains dried and ground blue fenugreek. This spicy herb makes the cheese green and gives it its strong smell.

95413.q: What happened in the town of Glarus in the canton of Glarus in 1861?
a: A big fire destroyed most of the town
95413.e: In 1861 a strong föhn wind drove a fire through the town. Afterwards Glarus was rebuilt with wide, straight streets.
95413.m: After the fire of 1861, Glarus was rebuilt.

95414.q: How do voters vote at the Landsgemeinde in Glarus?
a: By raising their hands in the open air
In the Federal Palace in Bern
95414.e: On the first Sunday in May, voters gather on the Zaunplatz in Glarus. There they vote in the open air by raising their hands.
95414.m: At the Glarus Landsgemeinde you vote by raising your hand.

95421.q: What is the capital of the canton of the Grisons?
95421.e: Chur is the capital of the Grisons. The town lies in the Rhine Valley.
95421.m: Chur is the capital of the Grisons.

95422.q: Which animal is the well-known heraldic animal of the canton of the Grisons and lives in the mountains?
95422.e: The ibex can be seen on the Grisons coat of arms. It climbs skilfully on steep rocks.
95422.m: The ibex is the heraldic animal of the Grisons.

95423.q: Which large park, where animals and plants live completely undisturbed, is in the canton of the Grisons?
95423.e: The Swiss National Park in the Engadine was founded in 1914. Animals and plants can live there completely undisturbed.
95423.m: Switzerland's only national park is in the Grisons.

95424.q: Which cake with walnuts and caramel is a speciality from the canton of the Grisons?
95424.e: The Grisons nut tart has a filling of walnuts and caramel. It is sweet and keeps for a long time.
95424.m: The nut tart comes from the Grisons.

95425.q: Which big river rises in the canton of the Grisons?
95425.e: The Anterior Rhine and the Posterior Rhine rise in the Grisons. At Reichenau they join to form the Rhine.
95425.m: The Rhine rises in the Grisons.

95426.q: What do children in the Engadine in the canton of the Grisons do at Chalandamarz, on 1 March?
a: They go through the village with bells to drive away winter
They build sandcastles by the lake
They look for Easter eggs in the forest
95426.e: At Chalandamarz, children go through the village with cowbells and songs. The noise is meant to drive winter away.
95426.m: At Chalandamarz, children ring winter away.

95427.q: What is the name of the boy in the famous children's book who fetches a big bell in the Engadine in the canton of the Grisons?
95427.e: Schellen-Ursli (known in English as “A Bell for Ursli”) fetches a big bell from the alpine hut so that he can walk at the front at Chalandamarz. The book is set in the village of Guarda.
95427.m: Schellen-Ursli is a boy from the Engadine.

95428.q: Which meat speciality from the canton of the Grisons is air-dried?
95428.e: Bündnerfleisch is beef that is seasoned and dried in the air. It is cut into very thin slices.

95429.q: Which river flows through the Engadine in the canton of the Grisons?
95429.e: The Inn rises near the Maloja Pass and flows through the whole Engadine. The name Engadine means valley of the Inn.
95429.m: The Engadine is the valley of the Inn.

95430.q: Which place in the canton of the Grisons hosted the Winter Olympics twice?
95430.e: St Moritz hosted the Winter Olympics in 1928 and 1948. The resort is world-famous for winter sports.
95430.m: St Moritz hosted the Winter Olympics twice.

95431.q: Which big meeting takes place every January in Davos in the canton of the Grisons?
a: The annual meeting of the World Economic Forum
95431.e: At the World Economic Forum, WEF for short, politicians and business leaders from all over the world meet. They talk about important questions for the future.
95431.m: In January the world meets at the WEF in Davos.

95432.q: What is the highest mountain in the canton of the Grisons called?
95432.e: Piz Bernina is 4,049 metres high. It is the only four-thousander in the Eastern Alps.
95432.m: Piz Bernina is the highest mountain in the Grisons.

95433.q: Through which tunnel does the car train go from Klosters to the Lower Engadine in the canton of the Grisons?
95433.e: The Vereina Tunnel opened in 1999. Cars are loaded onto the train and so travel under the mountains into the Engadine.
95433.m: The Vereina Tunnel links Klosters with the Engadine.

95434.q: Which pass links the canton of the Grisons with the canton of Ticino?
95434.e: Over the San Bernardino Pass and through the San Bernardino Tunnel you get from the Rheinwald into the Misox valley and on into Ticino.
95434.m: The San Bernardino leads from the Grisons to Ticino.

95435.q: Which famous train runs from Zermatt to St Moritz in the canton of the Grisons?
95435.e: The Glacier Express goes through many tunnels and over high bridges. It is known as the slowest express train in the world.
95435.m: The Glacier Express links Zermatt and St Moritz.

95436.q: Which three countries does the canton of the Grisons border?
95436.e: The Grisons is in the south-east of Switzerland. It borders Italy, Austria and Liechtenstein.
95436.m: The Grisons has three neighbouring countries: Italy, Austria and Liechtenstein.

95443.q: What is the capital of the canton of Jura?
95443.e: The capital of the canton of Jura is Delémont, Delsberg in German. The cantonal government and parliament meet there.

95444.q: Which language is mainly spoken in the canton of Jura?
95444.e: In the canton of Jura almost the whole population speaks French. It is part of western Switzerland, the Romandie.

95445.q: Which neighbouring country does the canton of Jura border?
95445.e: The canton of Jura is in the north-west of Switzerland and has a long border with France. It has no border with Italy, Austria or Germany.
95445.m: Jura is a neighbour of France.

95446.q: Which animal is especially famous in the Franches-Montagnes in the canton of Jura?
95446.e: Horses have been bred in the Franches-Montagnes for a long time. The Franches-Montagnes horse is strong, calm and friendly.
95446.m: Franches-Montagnes horses come from the Franches-Montagnes in Jura.

95447.q: What was found during the building of the motorway near Porrentruy in the canton of Jura?
95447.e: While building the A16 motorway, thousands of dinosaur footprints were discovered near Porrentruy. They are many millions of years old.

95448.q: What colours does the coat of arms of the canton of Jura have?
95448.e: The coat of arms of the canton of Jura is red and white. It shows a red bishop's crook and red and white stripes.
95448.m: The Jura coat of arms is red and white.

95449.q: Which river flows through the medieval little town of Saint-Ursanne in the canton of Jura?
95449.e: The Doubs winds through the canton of Jura and flows right past Saint-Ursanne. A beautiful old stone bridge crosses the river there.

95450.q: Which cheese, also made in the canton of Jura, is not cut but scraped into small rosettes with a crank?
95450.e: Tête de Moine is scraped into fine rosettes with a device called a girolle. It is made in the Jura arc, including the Franches-Montagnes in the canton of Jura.
95450.m: Tête de Moine is scraped, not cut.

95451.q: Which animals are the centre of attention at the Marché-Concours in the canton of Jura, a big festival every August?
95451.e: The Marché-Concours in Saignelégier is a famous horse festival with shows and horse races. The Franches-Montagnes horses are the centre of attention.
95451.m: At the Marché-Concours, everything is about Franches-Montagnes horses.

95452.q: What can be seen on the left side of the coat of arms of the canton of Jura?
95452.e: On the left, the coat of arms shows a red bishop's crook on a white background. It is a reminder that the area used to belong to the Prince-Bishop of Basel. On the right are red and white stripes.
95452.m: The bishop's crook on the Jura coat of arms recalls the Prince-Bishop of Basel.

95453.q: Who ruled the area of today's canton of Jura for centuries?
95453.e: The area of today's canton of Jura belonged for a long time to the Prince-Bishopric of Basel. The Prince-Bishop was both a church leader and a worldly ruler.
95453.m: Jura was once the land of the Prince-Bishop of Basel.

95454.q: A big castle stands above the old town of Porrentruy in the canton of Jura. Who used to live there?
95454.e: After the Reformation, the Prince-Bishops of Basel moved to Porrentruy. Porrentruy Castle still towers over the old town today.
95454.m: Porrentruy Castle was the seat of the Prince-Bishops.

95455.q: Why is the water of the Étang de la Gruère, a bog pond in the Franches-Montagnes, so dark?
a: Because of the peat from the bog
Because of oil in the water
95455.e: The Étang de la Gruère is a bog pond surrounded by forest and raised bog. The water is coloured dark by the peat.
95455.m: Peat colours the water of the Étang de la Gruère dark.

95456.q: The Jurassic is a period of Earth's history and is named after the Jura mountains. Which animals lived at that time?
95456.e: The Jurassic is named after the Jura mountains because typical rocks from this period were found there. Many dinosaurs lived at that time. Mammoths and cave bears only lived much later, in the Ice Age.
95456.m: Many dinosaurs lived in the Jurassic.

95457.q: What can you visit in Réclère in the canton of Jura?
95457.e: The Réclère caves are full of stalactites and stalagmites. Next to them there is a park with models of dinosaurs.
95457.m: In Réclère you go underground to see stalactites.

95458.q: What is the A16 motorway called that links the canton of Jura with Biel and with France?
95458.e: The A16 is called the Transjurane. It runs from Biel through the Jura to Boncourt on the French border.
95458.m: The Transjurane runs right across the Jura.

95465.q: Which lake is the city of Lucerne on?
95465.e: The city of Lucerne lies on Lake Lucerne. From there, boats go to many places around the lake.

95466.q: According to legend, which mythical creature lived on Mount Pilatus near Lucerne?
95466.e: Many legends tell of dragons that are said to have lived on Pilatus. That is why the dragon is still often seen there as a symbol today.
95466.m: In legends, dragons live on Pilatus.

95467.q: Which big museum in Lucerne shows locomotives, ships, aeroplanes and cars?
95467.e: The Swiss Museum of Transport in Lucerne is one of the most visited museums in Switzerland. There you learn all about transport by rail, road, water and air.
95467.m: At the Museum of Transport in Lucerne, everything is about transport.

95468.q: What colours does the coat of arms of the canton of Lucerne have?
95468.e: The Lucerne coat of arms is divided vertically: blue on the left, white on the right. It is one of the simplest coats of arms in Switzerland.

95469.q: Which colourful festival with Guggenmusik bands and masks is especially famous in Lucerne?
95469.e: Lucerne Carnival is one of the biggest in Switzerland. It begins early in the morning on “Dirty Thursday” with a loud bang.
95469.m: Lucerne celebrates a loud and colourful carnival.

95470.q: Which language is spoken in the canton of Lucerne?
95470.e: In the canton of Lucerne people speak German, usually the Lucerne dialect in everyday life. Lucerne is in central Switzerland.

95471.q: What is the octagonal tower called that stands in the water next to the Chapel Bridge in Lucerne?
95471.e: The Water Tower stands in the middle of the Reuss next to the Chapel Bridge. Together they are Lucerne's best-known landmark.
95471.m: The Chapel Bridge and Water Tower belong together.

95472.q: Which hard, ring-shaped biscuit comes from Willisau in the canton of Lucerne?
95472.e: Willisauer Ringli are small, very hard rings made of sugar and flour. You can suck on them for a long time.
95472.m: Willisauer Ringli are hard and sweet.

95473.q: What is special about the clock on the Zyt Tower in the Musegg Wall in Lucerne?
a: It may strike one minute before all the other clocks in the city
It has only one hour hand, made of gold
95473.e: The clock in the Zyt Tower is the oldest tower clock in Lucerne. That is why it has the privilege of striking one minute earlier than all the other clocks in the city.
95473.m: The Zyt Tower in Lucerne always strikes first.

95474.q: Which covered wooden bridge in Lucerne is decorated with paintings of a Dance of Death?
95474.e: The Spreuer Bridge is the second old wooden bridge over the Reuss in Lucerne. Its paintings show a Dance of Death from the 17th century.
95474.m: The Spreuer Bridge is the bridge with the Dance of Death.

95475.q: Which river flows out of Lake Lucerne in the city of Lucerne?
95475.e: In Lucerne the Reuss leaves Lake Lucerne. Later, in the canton of Aargau, it flows into the Aare.
95475.m: The Reuss flows right through Lucerne.

95476.q: Which region in the canton of Lucerne is a UNESCO biosphere reserve?
95476.e: The UNESCO Biosphere Entlebuch protects moors, forests and mountains. At the same time, farming and tourism in harmony with nature are encouraged there.
95476.m: The Entlebuch is a UNESCO biosphere.

95477.q: Which of these cantons does NOT border the canton of Lucerne?
95477.e: Lucerne borders Aargau, Zug, Schwyz, Nidwalden, Obwalden and Bern. Uri lies further south and is not a neighbour of Lucerne.
95477.m: Uri is not a neighbour of Lucerne.

95478.q: After the city of Lucerne, which municipality is the largest in the canton of Lucerne?
95478.e: Emmen lies right next to the city of Lucerne and has more than 30,000 inhabitants. That makes it the second-largest municipality in the canton.
95478.m: Emmen is the second-largest municipality in the canton of Lucerne.

95479.q: What is the name of the Lucerne speciality made of puff pastry filled with little meatballs in a cream sauce?
95479.e: The Chügelipastete is a large puff pastry with little meatballs and sauce. It is also called Fritschipastete.
95479.m: People in Lucerne love to eat Chügelipastete.

95480.q: Which modern building right on the lake in Lucerne is world-famous for its concert hall?
95480.e: The KKL (Culture and Convention Centre Lucerne) was designed by the French architect Jean Nouvel. Its large roof sticks out far over the lake.
95480.m: At the KKL Luzern, music sounds out by the lake.

95487.q: What is the capital of the canton of Neuchâtel?
95487.e: The capital is called Neuchâtel, in German Neuenburg. The town lies on Lake Neuchâtel.
95487.m: The canton and its capital are both called Neuchâtel.

95488.q: Which language is spoken in the canton of Neuchâtel?
95488.e: People in the canton of Neuchâtel speak French. It belongs to Romandy, the French-speaking part of Switzerland.

95489.q: On which large lake does the town of Neuchâtel lie?
95489.e: The town of Neuchâtel lies on the shore of Lake Neuchâtel. In good weather you can see as far as the Alps from the lake.

95490.q: Which three colours are on the coat of arms of the canton of Neuchâtel?
95490.e: The Neuchâtel coat of arms has three vertical stripes in green, white and red. At the top of the red stripe there is a small white cross.
95490.m: Neuchâtel wears green, white and red.

95491.q: What is the name of the huge rock amphitheatre in the canton of Neuchâtel where you often see ibex?
95491.e: The Creux du Van is an enormous rock bowl with almost vertical walls. Ibex and chamois live there.
95491.m: The Creux du Van is a huge rock amphitheatre.

95492.q: Which neighbouring country does the canton of Neuchâtel border?
95492.e: The canton of Neuchâtel lies in the Jura and borders France to the west. Part of the border is formed by the river Doubs.
95492.m: Neuchâtel is a neighbour of France.

95493.q: Which big festival does the town of Neuchâtel celebrate every year at the end of September?
a: The Fête des Vendanges (grape harvest festival)
95493.e: At the Fête des Vendanges, Neuchâtel celebrates the end of the grape harvest. There is a big parade with decorated floats and lots of music.
95493.m: At the end of September, Neuchâtel celebrates the Fête des Vendanges.

95494.q: What is the name of the waterfall on the Doubs on the border between the canton of Neuchâtel and France?
95494.e: At the Saut du Doubs, the Doubs plunges about 27 metres. You can reach the waterfall by boat from Les Brenets, for example.
95494.m: At the Saut du Doubs, the Doubs leaps into the depths.

95495.q: Which world-famous architect was born in La Chaux-de-Fonds in the canton of Neuchâtel in 1887?
95495.e: Le Corbusier's real name was Charles-Édouard Jeanneret, and he grew up in La Chaux-de-Fonds. He became one of the most important architects of the 20th century.
95495.m: Le Corbusier came from La Chaux-de-Fonds.

95496.q: Which famous racing driver and car maker was born in La Chaux-de-Fonds in 1878?
95496.e: Louis Chevrolet emigrated to the USA, where he co-founded the Chevrolet car brand. He was born in La Chaux-de-Fonds.
95496.m: Chevrolet has its roots in La Chaux-de-Fonds.

95497.q: Since which year has Neuchâtel been a canton of the Swiss Confederation?
95497.e: Neuchâtel was admitted to the Confederation as a canton in 1815. At the same time, until 1848 it remained a principality of the King of Prussia.
95497.m: Neuchâtel has been a Swiss canton since 1815.

95498.q: Why is 1 March a public holiday in the canton of Neuchâtel?
a: It commemorates the founding of the Republic of Neuchâtel in 1848
It commemorates the invention of the wristwatch
The grape harvest begins on this day
95498.e: On 1 March 1848, the people of Neuchâtel declared a republic. The canton has celebrated this day every year since.
95498.m: On 1 March, Neuchâtel celebrates its republic.

95499.q: Which museum in La Chaux-de-Fonds shows clocks and watches from many centuries?
95499.e: The Musée international d'horlogerie in La Chaux-de-Fonds shows thousands of clocks and watches. There you learn how timekeeping developed.
