97333.m: Manure is collected on the manure heap.

97334.q: Which machine does the farmer hitch to the tractor to spread manure on the field?
97334.e: The manure spreader is a trailer with turning rollers at the back. They throw the manure evenly over the field.
97334.m: Manure is spread on the field with the manure spreader.

97335.q: Which crispy breakfast flakes are made from maize?
97335.e: For cornflakes, maize is cooked, rolled flat and toasted. Here the word “corn” means maize.

97336.q: For which celebration do many Swiss farms invite people to a big breakfast?
97336.e: On the national holiday many farms hold the farmers' breakfast, the 1 August brunch. People eat plaited bread, cheese and butter from the farm.
97336.m: On 1 August many farms hold a brunch.

97337.q: What do cows get from sugar beet once the sugar has been extracted?
97337.e: After the sugar is extracted, small pieces of beet are left over. This pulp is good feed for cows.
97337.m: The leftovers of sugar beet are feed for cows.

97338.q: What is separating the grains from the stalks called?
97338.e: When threshing, the grains are beaten out of the ears. In the past this was done by hand with a flail.
97338.m: Threshing separates the grains from the straw.

97437.q: Where in the body do feelings like joy come from?
97437.e: The brain processes everything we experience. Our feelings come from there too.

97438.q: Which substances in the body are often called “happy hormones”?
97438.e: The body makes endorphins itself, for example during sport. They give you a good feeling.

97439.q: What do your arms often do when you are very happy, for example after a win?
a: They go up in the air
97439.e: Many athletes throw their arms up after a win. That way the whole body shows the joy.
97439.m: When happy, people often throw their arms up.

97440.q: What does a dog often do when it is happy?
97440.e: A happy dog wags its tail and often jumps around.
97440.m: A happy dog wags its tail.

97441.q: What does a cat often do when it is content?
97441.e: A cat that feels good makes a quiet, rumbling sound. This is called purring.

97442.q: What do you call a feeling of deep contentment and joy?
97442.e: Someone who is happy feels completely well and content.
97442.m: Happiness is a feeling of deep joy.

97443.q: What do many people do when they are in a good mood?
97443.e: A good mood often shows in cheerful sounds, for example singing or whistling.
97443.m: People in a good mood often sing.

97444.q: What helps many children when they are in a bad mood?
97444.e: Playing together takes your mind off things and often brings back the fun.
97444.m: Playing with friends chases away a bad mood.

97445.q: What does the body need so that you are in a good mood in the morning?
97445.e: During sleep the body recovers. If you have slept well, you start the day more cheerfully.
97445.m: Enough sleep puts you in a good mood.

97446.q: What colour do many people in Switzerland wear to a funeral?
97446.e: Here, black is the colour of mourning. In other countries it can be different.
97446.m: Here, black is the colour of mourning.

97447.q: What is the ceremony called where people say goodbye to someone who has died?
97447.e: At a funeral, family and friends come together to say goodbye.
97447.m: At a funeral, people say goodbye.

97448.q: What do people who are grieving often put on a grave?
97448.e: Flowers on a grave show that you are thinking of the person who has died.
97448.m: People often put flowers on graves.

97449.q: What do people often light to remember someone who has died?
97449.e: A burning candle is a sign of remembrance and hope.
97449.m: A candle helps people remember those who have died.

97450.q: How does the body often feel when someone is very sad after a loss?
97450.e: Grief takes a lot of strength. Many people feel exhausted then.

97451.q: What can help children when they are grieving for someone?
97451.e: Sharing memories keeps the person alive in your heart. That is comforting.

97452.q: What is the place where people who have died are buried called?
97452.e: The graves are in the cemetery. You can go there to remember people who have died.
97452.m: People who have died are buried in the cemetery.

97453.q: What does a flag that is only raised halfway show?
97453.e: A flag at half mast is a sign of mourning, for example after a disaster.
97453.m: A flag at half mast shows mourning.

97454.q: Which word means something like worry and sadness?
97454.e: Someone who feels sorrow is downhearted and has worries.

97455.q: What do many people do with their hands when they are angry?
97455.e: When you are angry, your body tenses up. Your hands often close tightly into fists.
97455.m: When angry, people often clench their fists.

97456.q: What happens to your muscles when you are angry?
97456.e: When you are angry, your body gets ready to act. The muscles become hard and tense.

97457.q: What does a dog often do when it is angry?
97457.e: By growling, a dog warns: do not come too close!

97458.q: What does a cat do when it is angry or threatening?
97458.e: An angry cat hisses loudly and shows its teeth.

97459.q: How can you get rid of anger with your body without doing any harm?
97459.e: Movement releases the tension in the body. Afterwards you often feel calmer.
97459.m: Running helps you get rid of anger.

97460.q: How do people often speak when they are angry?
97460.e: When you are angry, your voice often gets louder and sharper.

97461.q: What does it mean if someone is “hot under the collar”?
97461.e: Someone who is hot under the collar can hardly hold back their annoyance any more.
97461.m: Someone hot under the collar is very angry.

97462.q: What do people often do with their teeth when they are angry?
97462.e: When you are angry, your jaw muscles tense too. That is why you press your teeth together.
97462.m: When angry, people clench their teeth.

97463.q: What helps you calm down again after an argument?
97463.e: A short break gives the body time to calm down.
97463.m: A break calms you down after an argument.

97464.q: What often happens to your hands when you are very frightened?
97464.e: When you are afraid, the body works at full speed. Your hands often get damp.
97464.m: When you are afraid, your hands often sweat.

97465.q: Where do many people feel excitement or fear especially clearly?
97465.e: Before a test, many people have a queasy or heavy feeling in their tummy.
97465.m: You often feel fear in your tummy.

97466.q: Which substance gets the body ready to run away when you are afraid?
97466.e: Adrenaline is released when there is danger. It makes the body alert and fast.
97466.m: Adrenaline gets the body ready in danger.

97467.q: What does a roe deer do when it senses danger?
97467.e: Roe deer are animals that flee. When there is danger, they leap away quickly.

97468.q: How do your knees sometimes feel when you are very frightened?
97468.e: People then say they feel weak at the knees. The legs shake with excitement.
97468.m: When frightened, you go weak at the knees.

97469.q: What is a jokey name for someone who gets scared easily?
97469.e: People jokingly call someone who is easily frightened a scaredy-cat. In German they say “scared hare”, because hares are very jumpy.

97470.q: What is fear of a school test called?
97470.e: Many people are nervous before a test. Learning well can help make the fear smaller.
97470.m: Many people get exam nerves before tests.

97471.q: What is the fear of looking down from a high tower called?
97471.e: With a fear of heights, you feel uneasy or dizzy when you are high up.
97471.m: Someone afraid of being high up has a fear of heights.

97472.q: What does your mouth often do when you are surprised?
97472.e: When you are surprised, your lower jaw drops a little. Your mouth opens into an “Oh”.

97473.q: What is true about the feeling of surprise?
a: It usually only lasts a short time
It only comes in your sleep
97473.e: A surprise is over quickly. Another feeling often follows.
97473.m: Surprise only lasts a short time.

97474.q: What do people often say when they are surprised?
97474.e: “Oh!” is a typical cry of surprise.

97475.q: What is a party called that the person being celebrated knows nothing about beforehand?
97475.e: For a surprise party, everyone prepares everything in secret.
97475.m: A surprise party is prepared in secret.

97476.q: Which feelings can follow a surprise?
97476.e: A nice surprise makes you happy, a spooky one makes you afraid.
97476.m: Joy or fear often follow a surprise.

97477.q: What does the saying “My jaw dropped” mean?
97477.e: When you are amazed, your mouth opens wide. That is why people say their jaw dropped.
97477.m: If your jaw drops, you are very surprised.

97478.q: What do you call a sudden, unpleasant surprise?
97478.e: A loud bang behind your back can give you a fright.
97478.m: A fright is an unpleasant surprise.

97479.q: What is it called when you are full of wonder about something?
97479.e: Someone who marvels is surprised and amazed by something new.
97479.m: Someone who marvels is full of wonder.

97480.q: Why is the feeling of disgust useful?
a: It protects you from spoiled food
97480.e: Disgust stops us from eating things that could make us ill.
97480.m: Disgust protects you from spoiled food.

97481.q: Which word do people often say when they are disgusted?
97481.e: People say “yuck” or “ew” when they find something disgusting.

97482.q: What do you usually do when you have something disgusting in your mouth?
97482.e: Disgust makes you want to get rid of inedible things at once. That way they do not reach your stomach.
97482.m: You usually spit out disgusting things.

97483.q: What can you sometimes get when you feel strong disgust?
97483.e: Strong disgust can make you feel sick. Sometimes you even gag.
97483.m: Strong disgust can make you feel sick.

97484.q: What do many people find disgusting?
97484.e: Mould can be poisonous. That is why most people find it disgusting.
97484.m: Many people are disgusted by mould.

97485.q: Which sense organ often warns us first about spoiled food?
97485.e: Spoiled food smells bad. That is why you often notice it first with your nose.
97485.m: The nose warns you about spoiled food.

97486.q: Which animals have been allowed as food in Switzerland since 2017, even though many people find them disgusting?
97486.e: Since 2017, mealworms, crickets and migratory locusts may be sold as food in Switzerland. In other countries people have eaten insects for a long time.
97486.m: In Switzerland you are allowed to eat some insects.

97487.q: What do you find on old bread when it has gone mouldy?
97487.e: Mould grows as a fluffy layer, often green, white or black. You do not eat bread like that any more.

97488.q: What do many people feel in their body before they do something brave?
97488.e: Before a brave act you are excited. Your heart then beats noticeably.
97488.m: Before brave acts, your heart often pounds.

97489.q: What do you need to jump off the three-metre board for the first time?
97489.e: From up high, the water looks far away. It takes courage to jump anyway.
97489.m: You need courage for a high jump.

97490.q: Who often rescues people who have had accidents in the Swiss mountains by helicopter?
97490.e: Rega, the Swiss Air Rescue, flies to injured people by helicopter. The crews also fly in difficult conditions.

97491.q: What do you say to give someone courage?
97491.e: Encouraging words give strength and confidence.

97492.q: What is someone like who has lost all their courage?
97492.e: Someone who is discouraged no longer believes they can do anything and has no hope.
97492.m: Someone who has lost their courage is discouraged.

97493.e: Reckless children are so wild that they sometimes overlook dangers.
97493.m: You are reckless when you are too wild.

97494.q: What does the saying “pluck up the courage” mean?
97494.e: Someone who plucks up the courage overcomes their fear and does something brave.
97494.m: If you pluck up the courage, you become brave.

a: A task where you have to show courage
97495.e: In a dare you are meant to prove that you are brave enough to do something. But you should say no to dangerous dares.
97495.m: In a dare you are meant to prove your courage.

a: Fear that someone else is preferred
97496.e: Someone who is jealous fears getting less love or attention than someone else.
97496.m: Jealousy is the fear of getting less attention.

97497.q: When do children often get jealous?
a: When a brother or sister gets a lot of attention
97497.e: A new baby brother or sister needs a lot of care. Older children then sometimes feel left out.
97497.m: Brothers and sisters can be jealous of each other.

97498.q: Which colour appears in the saying for strong envy?
97498.e: People say: “He is green with envy.”
97498.m: People say someone is green with envy.

97499.e: If you talk about your feelings, you can find a solution together with others.

97500.q: What does it mean to be happy for someone?
a: To take it away from them
To laugh at them for it
97500.e: If you are happy for someone, you share their joy when they get something nice. That is the opposite of envy.
97500.m: Being happy for others means sharing their joy.

97501.q: Which pet showed jealousy in a study when its owner stroked a toy dog?
97501.e: Researchers saw that the dogs then pushed in and shoved the toy dog away.

97502.q: What does a jealous child often want?
a: To go to bed at once
97502.e: Jealous children want to show: I am still here too.

97503.q: Who knows the feeling of jealousy?
97503.e: Jealousy is a completely normal feeling. Almost everyone feels it at some point.

97504.q: What is hardly possible while laughing loudly?
97504.e: When you laugh, you keep pushing air out. That is why you can hardly speak at the same time.
97504.m: While laughing you can hardly speak.

97505.q: What are the clowns of the Theodora Foundation who make children laugh in Swiss hospitals called?
97505.e: The Dream Doctors visit sick children in hospital and bring fun into their day.
97505.m: Dream Doctors make sick children laugh.

97506.q: Who makes people laugh at the circus?
97506.e: The clown does funny things and trips over on purpose. The audience then laughs.
97506.m: At the circus, the clown makes everyone laugh.

97507.q: What do you tell to make others laugh?
97507.e: A joke is a short, funny story with a surprising punchline.
97507.m: You make others laugh with a joke.

97508.q: How does the body often feel after a good laugh?
97508.e: Laughing releases tension in the body. Afterwards many people feel loose and good.

97509.q: What is the difference between smiling and laughing?
a: When you laugh you make sounds
When you smile you make noise
When you laugh your mouth stays shut
97509.e: A smile is silent. When you laugh, you hear sounds like “hee hee” or “ha ha”.
97509.m: You hear laughing, but you only see smiling.

97510.q: Which animal makes sounds that sound like loud laughter?
97510.e: The spotted hyena in Africa giggles and cackles loudly. It uses these sounds to communicate with other hyenas.
97510.m: The calls of the spotted hyena sound like laughter.

97511.q: The laughing kookaburra is a bird whose call sounds like loud laughter. Where does it live?
97511.e: The laughing kookaburra is a large kingfisher from Australia. Its call sounds like wild laughter.
97511.m: The laughing kookaburra lives in Australia.

97512.q: What are tears that you cry out of sheer joy called?
97512.e: Great joy can make you cry too, for example when you see someone again.
97512.m: When you are very happy, you cry tears of joy.

97513.e: Crocodile tears are false tears. The person is not really sad at all.
97513.m: Crocodile tears are only pretend tears.

97514.q: Which word describes very heavy, sad crying?
97514.e: People say: “She is crying bitterly.” That means someone is very sad and crying hard.
97514.m: Someone who cries bitterly is very sad.

97515.q: How do babies who cannot speak yet show that something is wrong?
97515.e: Babies cry when they are hungry, tired or in pain.
97515.m: Babies show what is wrong by crying.

97516.q: Why do you cry when you cut onions?
a: A substance from the onion irritates the eyes
97516.e: When you cut an onion, a substance escapes into the air. It irritates the eyes, and they wash it away with tears.
97516.m: Onions irritate the eyes and make them water.

97517.e: Crying is normal for everyone, whether child or adult, boy or girl.

97518.q: What do you call the jerky breathing when you cry hard?
97518.e: When you sob, you breathe in with sudden jerks. This often happens when you cry hard.
97518.m: When you cry hard, you sob.

97519.q: What do your eyes often look like after crying for a long time?
97519.e: Crying for a long time irritates the eyes. They turn red and the eyelids swell.
97519.m: After crying for a long time, your eyes are often red.

97520.q: What do people often hand to someone who is crying?
97520.e: With a tissue you can dry your tears. It is a small, kind gesture.
97520.m: You hand a crying person a tissue.

a: A prize to comfort the losers
97521.e: People who did not win sometimes get a small consolation prize. That makes the disappointment smaller.
97521.m: A consolation prize comforts the losers.

97522.q: What comforts many small children when they fall asleep?
97522.e: A soft cuddly toy makes small children feel safe and secure.

97523.q: What is especially important when comforting someone?
97523.e: If you listen, you show the other person that their worries matter.
97523.m: When comforting someone, you listen well.

97524.q: Which substance is released in the body when you cuddle and is called the “cuddle hormone”?
97524.e: Oxytocin is produced during a hug, for example. It calms you and gives a feeling of closeness.
97524.m: Oxytocin is also called the cuddle hormone.

97525.q: What do parents often do when a small child has hurt their knee?
97525.e: Blowing distracts the child and shows care. That comforts small children.
97525.m: Blowing on a hurt comforts small children.

97526.e: Nice thoughts and memories make your heart feel lighter.

97527.q: Which animals visit people in care homes or hospitals to comfort and calm them?
97527.e: Specially trained therapy dogs let people stroke them. That does many people good.

97528.q: How do you feel when you have managed something difficult?
97528.e: If you master a difficult task, you are pleased with yourself. This feeling is called pride.
97528.m: After a success you feel proud.

97529.q: How do people often hold their body when they are proud?
a: Upright with their head held high
97529.e: Proud people stand up straight and lift their chin.

97530.q: Which bird appears in the saying “as proud as a ...”?
97530.e: The peacock spreads its magnificent feathers in a fan. That is why people say “as proud as a peacock”.
97530.m: People say as proud as a peacock.

97531.q: What is the feeling called when you are ashamed of something?
97531.e: Shame is the opposite of pride. You would rather hide.
97531.m: Someone who is ashamed feels shame.

97533.q: What can parents say when their child has done something well?
97533.e: Praise shows that someone has noticed and values what you have done.

97534.q: What do you call too much pride, where you look down on others?
97534.e: Arrogance means thinking you are better than others. The saying goes: “Pride comes before a fall.”
97534.m: Too much pride is called arrogance.

97535.q: When is it right to be proud?
a: When you have learnt something by practising
97535.e: If you have practised hard and succeed, you can be proud of yourself.
97535.m: You can be proud of your own achievements.

98129.e: Wheat is a cereal. Its grains are made into flour for bread.
98129.m: Wheat is the most important bread cereal.

98130.q: Which of these plants is a cereal?
98130.e: Barley is a cereal like wheat, rye and oats. Potato, carrot and pea are vegetables.
98130.m: Barley, rye and oats are cereals.

98131.q: What is a field where grain is grown called?
98131.e: An arable field is a field that is ploughed and planted. On a pasture, by contrast, animals eat grass.

98132.q: What was a flail used for in the past?
a: To beat grains out of the ears
98132.e: With the flail, people beat the ears lying on the floor. This knocked the grains out.
98132.m: In the past, grain was threshed with a flail.

98133.q: Which cereal is polenta cooked from?
98133.e: Polenta is a porridge made from maize semolina. It is especially popular in Ticino.

98134.q: What is left of the grain stalks after threshing?
98134.e: The dry stalks without grains are called straw. Farmers use it, for example, as bedding in the barn.
98134.m: Straw is the dry stalks of cereals.

98135.q: Which cereal is grown most in Switzerland?
98135.e: Wheat grows most on Swiss fields. It is mainly used to make bread.
98135.m: Wheat is grown most in Switzerland.

98136.q: From which part of a cereal grain does a new plant grow?
98136.e: The germ holds the tiny new plant. When the grain gets into damp soil, it starts to grow.
98136.m: The germ is the baby plant in the grain.

98137.q: What does a cereal grain need in the soil to sprout?
98137.e: A grain needs water and warmth to sprout. Then a root and a stalk grow.

98138.q: What is an ear of grain?
98138.e: The ear sits at the top of the grain stalk. The grains grow tightly packed inside it.
98138.m: The grains sit in the ear.

98139.q: What are the long bristles on some ears of grain called?
98139.e: Awns are long, thin bristles on the grains. They stick far out of the ear.
98139.m: The bristles on the ear are called awns.

98140.q: Which cereal has especially long awns?
98140.e: Because of its long awns, an ear of barley looks almost like a paintbrush.
98140.m: You can recognise barley by its long awns.

98141.q: Oats have no ear. What is their flower head called?
98141.e: In oats, the grains hang singly on fine little branches. This kind of flower head is called a panicle.
98141.m: Oats carry their grains in a panicle.

98142.q: What colour is a ripe ear of wheat?
98142.e: Young ears are green. When they are ripe and dry, they turn golden yellow.

98143.q: Which cereal plant carries its grains on a cob?
98143.e: In maize, the grains sit in rows on a thick cob. Wheat, barley and rye have ears.
98143.m: Maize kernels grow on a cob.

98144.q: Why do ripe ears of grain often hang down?
98144.e: When the grains are ripe and plump, the ear becomes heavy. That is why the stalk bends down.
98144.m: Full ears are heavy and droop.

98145.q: What are the grains in the ear for the plant?
98145.e: The grains are the seeds of the cereal. A new plant can grow from every grain.

98146.q: What is made from cereal grains in a mill?
98146.e: In the mill, the grains are ground finely. This makes flour.
98146.m: In the mill, grain is ground into flour.

98147.q: What is the job of someone who grinds grain called?
98147.e: The miller grinds the grain into flour in the mill. The baker then bakes bread from it.
98147.m: The miller grinds, the baker bakes.

98148.q: What used to turn a mill by a stream?
98148.e: The flowing water turned a big wheel. This wheel drove the millstones.
98148.m: A watermill uses the power of water.

98149.q: What is a mill with big sails that turn in the wind called?
98149.e: In a windmill, the wind blows into the sails. This turns the mill without electricity.
98149.m: A windmill is driven by the wind.

98150.q: What was used to grind the grain in old mills?
98150.e: Two heavy, round stones lay on top of each other. The upper one turned and ground the grains.
98150.m: In the past, heavy millstones ground the grain.

98151.q: What do modern mills mostly use to grind grain?
98151.e: Today the grains pass between smooth or grooved steel rollers. This is fast and very fine.
98151.m: Modern mills grind with steel rollers.

98152.q: What are the bits of husk left over from milling called?
98152.e: Bran is made of the outer layers of the grains. For white flour it is separated out.
98152.m: Bran is the ground outer layer of the grain.

98153.q: What does the mill do with the grain before grinding it?
98153.e: First, little stones, dust and other seeds are removed. Only then does the clean grain go for grinding.

98154.q: What is coarsely ground grain, for example for a pudding, called?
98154.e: Semolina is coarser than flour. It is used to cook semolina pudding with milk, for example.
98154.m: Semolina is ground more coarsely than flour.

98155.e: To make flour, cereal grains are ground, for example wheat or spelt.

98156.q: Why is white flour so pale?
a: The outer layer has been removed
98156.e: For white flour only the pale inside of the grain is used. The dark outer layer is separated out.
98156.m: White flour is pale because the outer layer is missing.

98157.q: In Switzerland, what is the dark flour used to bake Ruchbrot called?
98157.e: Ruchmehl contains more of the outer layer than white flour. That is why it is darker.
98157.m: The dark Ruchbrot is baked from Ruchmehl.

98158.q: Which flour is between white flour and Ruchmehl in colour?
98158.e: Half-white flour is a bit darker than white flour but paler than Ruchmehl. It is often used for bread.

98159.q: What is flour mainly made of?
98159.e: Flour consists mostly of starch. It gives the body energy.

98160.q: What is the best way to store flour?
98160.e: Damp flour can go mouldy. If it is well sealed, no small creatures can get in either.
98160.m: Flour must be stored dry and sealed.

98161.q: Which small creature likes to live in old flour supplies?
98161.e: The mealworm is the larva of a beetle. It eats flour and grain.

98162.q: What do you make in a frying pan from flour, eggs and milk?
98162.e: Flour, eggs and milk make a runny batter. It is cooked thinly in the pan.
98162.m: Pancakes are made from flour, eggs and milk.

98163.q: What happens when you stir a little flour into a sauce?
98163.e: When cooked, the starch in the flour binds the water. That is why the sauce gets thicker.

98164.e: For wholemeal flour the whole grain is ground, with its outer layer and germ.
98164.m: Wholemeal means the whole grain is in it.

98165.q: What does wholemeal bread do compared with white bread?
a: It keeps you full for longer
98165.e: The body digests the fibre in wholemeal slowly. That is why you stay full for longer.
98165.m: Wholemeal bread keeps you full for a long time.

98166.q: Where in the grain are there lots of vitamins and minerals?
a: In the outer layer and germ
98166.e: The outer layers and the germ are especially rich in vitamins. In wholemeal bread they are kept.
98166.m: The outer layer and germ are full of vitamins.

98167.q: How can you often recognise wholemeal bread?
a: By bits of husk in the bread
By a hole in the middle
98167.e: In wholemeal bread you often see small dark bits. These are pieces of the grain's outer layer.
98167.m: You can see bits of husk in wholemeal bread.

98168.q: Which bread does the Swiss food pyramid especially recommend?
98168.e: The food pyramid advises choosing wholemeal cereal products. They contain more valuable nutrients.

98169.q: What does yeast do in bread dough?
98169.e: Yeast forms small gas bubbles in the dough. This makes the dough bigger and lighter.

98170.q: What does the yeast produce in the dough that puffs it up?
98170.e: The yeast produces the gas carbon dioxide. It makes lots of small bubbles in the dough.
98170.m: The yeast's gas bubbles make the dough big.

98171.q: Where does a yeast dough rise best?
98171.e: Yeast works best in warmth. In the cold the dough rises only very slowly.

98172.q: What is yeast that you buy as a powder in a sachet called?
98172.e: Dried yeast is yeast that has been dried. It keeps much longer than fresh yeast in a block.
98172.m: Dried yeast is yeast as a powder.

98173.q: What does the yeast in the dough feed on?
98173.e: The yeast eats sugar that comes from the starch in the flour. In doing so it produces gas.

98174.q: Where do the many holes in bread come from?
98174.e: Gas bubbles form while the dough rises. When it bakes, the dough sets and the holes stay.
98174.m: The holes in bread are gas bubbles.

98175.q: What happens to the yeast in the hot oven?
98175.e: The heat in the oven kills the yeast. That is why the bread stops rising after that.
98175.m: Yeast dies in the hot oven.

98176.q: Instead of shop-bought yeast, what can you use to make bread rise?
98176.e: Sourdough is an old, fermenting dough. It makes bread rise and gives it a slightly sour taste.

98177.q: Which four ingredients does a simple bread dough need?
98177.e: For a simple bread, flour, water, salt and yeast are enough. Other ingredients are not needed.
98177.m: Bread needs flour, water, salt and yeast.

98178.q: What do you do with bread dough to make it nice and stretchy?
98178.e: Kneading makes the dough smooth and stretchy. That way it can rise well later.
98178.m: Bread dough must be kneaded well.

98179.q: What does a yeast dough do when it rests covered?
98179.e: During the resting time the yeast works. The dough grows to about twice its size.

98180.q: What do you add when the dough sticks to your hands too much?
a: A little oil in the dough
98180.e: Flour soaks up moisture. That is why the dough sticks less afterwards.
98180.m: A little flour helps against sticky dough.

98181.q: What do you use to roll dough out flat?
98181.e: A rolling pin is a roller made of wood. You use it to roll the dough out thinly.
98181.m: A rolling pin makes dough flat.

98182.q: What do you usually cover dough with while it rises?
98182.e: A cloth keeps the dough warm and stops its surface drying out.
98182.m: A cloth protects the dough while it rises.

98183.q: What is the hard, brown outer layer of a loaf called?
98183.e: During baking, the surface of the dough gets hot and dry. This forms the crispy crust.
98183.m: The crust is on the outside of the bread.

98184.q: What is the soft inside of a loaf called?
98184.e: The crumb is the soft, light part of the bread. You can see the holes from rising in it.
98184.m: Inside the bread is the soft crumb.

98185.q: On which day do people in Switzerland traditionally eat Zopf, a plaited loaf, for breakfast?
98185.e: Zopf is the typical Sunday bread in Switzerland. People like to eat it with butter and jam.
98185.m: Zopf is the Swiss Sunday bread.

98186.q: What goes into Zopf dough but not into a simple bread?
98186.e: Zopf dough is made with milk and butter. That is why Zopf is soft and tastes delicious.

98187.q: What do you brush on the Zopf before baking to make it shiny?
98187.e: Beaten egg is brushed onto the Zopf. In the oven it then turns golden brown and shiny.
98187.m: Brushed with egg, the Zopf shines.

98188.q: How does the Zopf get its shape?
a: It is pressed into a tin
It is rolled into a ball
98188.e: Long strands are formed from the dough. These are plaited together like hair.
98188.m: A Zopf is plaited from strands of dough.

98190.q: Which figure made of sweet yeast dough is baked in Switzerland for St Nicholas Day?
98190.e: The Grittibänz is a little man made of yeast dough, similar to Zopf dough. People eat it around 6 December.
98190.m: On St Nicholas Day there is a Grittibänz.

98191.e: Zopf is a yeast dough. The yeast makes it light and airy.

98192.q: What is the Zopf named after?
98192.e: The loaf looks like plaited hair. In German this hairstyle is also called Zopf.
98192.m: The Zopf looks like plaited hair.

98193.q: Which cereal is spelt closely related to?
98193.e: Spelt is a close relative of wheat. It can be used for baking in a similar way.
98193.m: Spelt is a relative of wheat.

98195.q: What still has to be removed from spelt after threshing?
98195.e: In spelt, the grains stay firmly inside their husks. They have to be removed separately in the mill.
98195.m: Spelt grains sit in tough husks.

98196.q: What is spelt called that is harvested unripe and dried?
98196.e: Green spelt is spelt harvested when half ripe. It is dried and tastes a little smoky.
98196.m: Green spelt is spelt harvested unripe.

98197.q: How long has spelt been grown?
98197.e: Spelt has been grown for thousands of years. It also has a long tradition in Switzerland.

98198.q: What are the tough husks around the spelt grain for?
98198.e: The husks wrap the grain like a protective jacket. They are only removed in the mill.
98198.m: The husks protect the spelt grain.

98199.q: What can you bake with spelt flour?
98199.e: Spelt flour is good for baking. It is used to make bread, Zopf and biscuits.
98199.m: Spelt flour is good for baking.

98200.q: Where does rice very often grow?
98200.e: Many rice fields stand under water. Rice needs a lot of water and warmth.
98200.m: Rice often grows in fields under water.

98201.q: In which canton is the best-known rice field in Switzerland?
98201.e: Rice has been grown near Ascona in Ticino since the 1990s. It is one of the most northerly rice fields in the world.

98202.q: Which dish is cooked with rice?
98202.e: Risotto is a creamy rice dish from Italy that is also popular in Ticino. Polenta is made from maize.

98203.q: What is cooked from rice, milk and sugar?
98203.e: For rice pudding, rice is cooked slowly in milk. With sugar and cinnamon it becomes sweet.
98203.m: Rice pudding is sweet rice in milk.

98204.q: Which group of plants does rice belong to?
98204.e: Rice is a cereal, just like wheat. Its grains grow in a panicle.

98205.q: What is rice called that still has its brown outer layer?
98205.e: Brown rice only has its outermost husk removed. The brown layer stays on.

98206.q: What do people in many Asian countries eat rice with?
98206.e: In China, Japan and Korea people often eat with two chopsticks. You can eat rice well with them too.
98206.m: In East Asia people eat with chopsticks.

98207.q: What do millet grains look like?
98207.e: Millet grains are tiny, round and usually pale yellow. They are much smaller than wheat grains.

98208.q: Where is millet an especially important food today?
98208.e: Millet grows even where it is hot and dry. That is why it is very important in Africa and parts of Asia.
98208.m: Millet grows even in heat and drought.

98209.q: Which cereal can people eat who must not eat gluten?
98209.e: Millet contains no gluten, a protein found in wheat, spelt or barley. Some people get ill from it.

98210.q: What does the magic pot cook in the fairy tale “Sweet Porridge”?
98210.e: In the Brothers Grimm fairy tale, a little pot cooks so much millet porridge that the whole town fills up with it.
98210.m: The fairy tale “Sweet Porridge” is about millet porridge.

98211.q: What did many people in Switzerland often eat made from millet in the past?
98211.e: Before the potato arrived, millet porridge was an important food. Millet is easy to cook.
98211.m: In the past, people often ate millet porridge.

98212.q: Which pets like to nibble at millet sprays?
98212.e: Millet sprays are a popular food for pet birds. The birds peck off the small grains.

a: It is roasted in the oven
98213.e: Millet is cooked in water, similar to rice. Afterwards it is soft and fluffy.

98214.q: Apart from millet grains, what else made from millet can you buy?
98214.e: Millet is also rolled into flakes, similar to oats. You can add them to muesli.

98215.e: The oat grains are warmed and then pressed flat between rollers. This makes flakes.
98215.m: Oat flakes are oat grains rolled flat.

98216.q: Which Swiss breakfast is made with oat flakes and apples?
98216.e: For Bircher muesli, oat flakes are mixed with grated apple, milk or yoghurt.
98216.m: Bircher muesli is made with oat flakes.

98217.q: Which Swiss doctor is Bircher muesli named after?
98217.e: The Zurich doctor Maximilian Bircher-Benner made muesli well known around 1900.
98217.m: Bircher muesli comes from the doctor Bircher-Benner.

98218.q: What is a warm dish of oat flakes cooked in milk called?
98218.e: Porridge is an oat dish. It is a popular breakfast, especially in Great Britain.
98218.m: Porridge is warm oat flakes cooked in milk.

98219.q: Which animal traditionally likes to eat oats?
98219.e: Oats are a classic food for horses. They give them a lot of strength.

98220.q: What are oat flakes made from whole grains called?
98220.e: Jumbo flakes are rolled from whole grains. Fine flakes are made from chopped grains.
98220.m: Jumbo flakes are made from whole oat grains.

98221.q: Why are oat flakes considered a wholegrain product?
a: They contain a lot of sugar
98221.e: For oat flakes, the whole grain with its germ and outer layers is rolled. Only the outer husk is removed.
98221.m: Oat flakes contain the whole grain.

98222.q: What happens to oat flakes when you soak them in milk?
98222.e: The flakes soak up the milk and swell. This makes them soft.

98223.q: What can you bake from oat flakes, butter and sugar?
98223.e: Oat flakes are good for crunchy biscuits. They are mixed with butter, sugar and flour.
98223.m: You can bake biscuits from oat flakes.

98315.q: How do you often notice that you are tired?
98315.e: When the body needs sleep, the eyelids get heavy and almost close by themselves.
98315.m: Heavy eyes show you that you need sleep.

98316.q: What helps best against tiredness in the evening?
98316.e: Only real sleep helps against tiredness. During sleep, the body and brain recover.
98316.m: If you are tired, you should go to bed.

98317.q: How do you often feel when you have not slept enough?
98317.e: Too little sleep makes you tired and often irritable too. You have less strength and patience.
98317.m: Too little sleep makes you tired and grumpy.

98318.q: What often happens at school when you are very tired?
a: You find it hard to concentrate
98318.e: A tired brain works more slowly. You cannot pay attention as well and remember less.

98319.q: Which drink contains caffeine, which keeps you awake and is not good for children?
98319.e: Cola contains caffeine. Caffeine keeps you awake and can make it harder to fall asleep.
98319.m: The caffeine in cola keeps you awake.

98320.q: Why is it dangerous to ride a bike when you are very tired?
98320.e: If you are tired, you react more slowly and miss dangers more easily. That can lead to accidents in traffic.
98320.m: When tired, you react too slowly in traffic.

98321.q: What does your body do while you sleep?
98321.e: During sleep the body rests and repairs itself. In the morning you are refreshed again.
98321.m: Your body recovers while you sleep.

98322.q: What is the hormone that makes us tired in the evening called?
98322.e: Melatonin is made in the body when it is dark. It tells the body that it is time to sleep.

98323.q: How can you tell that you have had enough sleep?
a: You wake up fit in the morning
You are very tired at lunchtime
98323.e: If you sleep enough, you wake up refreshed and stay awake and lively during the day.
98323.m: If you sleep enough, you are fit in the morning.

98324.q: What do you call a short sleep in the middle of the day?
98324.e: An afternoon nap is a short sleep after lunch. Many small children have one every day.
98324.m: A short sleep in the middle of the day is a nap.

98325.q: In which country is the “siesta”, a midday rest, especially well known?
98325.e: The siesta is a midday rest in Spain. Many people rest there during the hot middle of the day.
98325.m: The siesta is the Spanish midday rest.

98326.q: Who most often needs an afternoon nap?
98326.e: Toddlers need a great deal of sleep. That is why they usually sleep in the middle of the day too.

98327.q: Roughly how long should a short nap for adults last?
98327.e: A short nap of about 10 to 30 minutes is refreshing. If you sleep longer, you often wake up groggy.
98327.m: A short nap only lasts about 20 minutes.

98328.q: Why should a nap not be too long?
a: Otherwise you find it harder to fall asleep at night
Otherwise you get ill straight away
98328.e: If you sleep a long time during the day, you are less tired in the evening. Then falling asleep is harder.
98328.m: A long nap disturbs your night's sleep.

98329.q: What is another word for a short sleep during the day?
98329.e: A nap is a short, light sleep during the day. You often nod off.
98329.m: A nap is a short sleep.

98330.q: Up to what age do most children have an afternoon nap?
98330.e: Most children stop having an afternoon nap between 3 and 5. Then the sleep at night is enough for them.
98330.m: At about 3 to 5, children stop having an afternoon nap.

98331.q: Which place is good for a nap?
a: A room with a loud television
98331.e: Quiet and little light help you fall asleep. Noise and bright light keep you awake.
98331.m: Quiet and darkness help with a nap.

98332.q: When do children often have more nightmares?
a: When they have had a bath
98332.e: Worries and excitement keep the brain busy at night too. That is why nightmares happen more often at such times.
98332.m: If you have worries, you have bad dreams more often.

98333.q: What can you do if you wake up after a nightmare?
98333.e: Parents can comfort and calm you. Afterwards you can usually fall asleep again easily.
98333.m: After a nightmare, it is fine to look for comfort.

98334.q: Do many children sometimes have nightmares?
98334.e: Almost all children have nightmares now and then. That is normal and not dangerous.
98334.m: Nightmares are completely normal in children.

98335.q: Is a monster from a nightmare real?
a: Yes, it lives under the bed
98335.e: Dreams happen in your head. What you dream has not really happened.
98335.m: What you dream is not real.

98336.q: What helps you calm down after a nightmare?
98336.e: Calm, deep breathing relaxes the body. Your heart then beats more slowly again.
98336.m: Deep breathing calms you after a nightmare.

98337.e: A nightmare is a dream that frightens you. You often wake up from it with a start.
98337.m: A nightmare is a dream that frightens you.

98338.q: What can cause nightmares in the evening?
98338.e: Scary pictures stay in your head. At night they can turn up again in dreams.
98338.m: Scary films in the evening can bring nightmares.

98339.q: Where does the “mare” in “nightmare” come from?
a: From a night spirit in old legends
98339.e: In old legends, a mare was a night spirit. People believed it sat on the chest of sleeping people at night.
98339.m: In old legends, the mare was a night spirit.

98340.q: What do you call the loud, rumbling breathing noise during sleep?
98340.e: When you snore, breathing during sleep makes a loud, rumbling noise.
98340.m: Loud breathing in your sleep is called snoring.

98341.q: Why does snoring make a noise?
98341.e: During sleep, the muscles in the throat relax. The air makes soft parts of the throat flutter, and that makes the noise.
98341.m: When you snore, soft parts of the throat flutter.

98342.q: When do people snore more often?
98342.e: If your nose is blocked, you breathe through your mouth. Then you snore more easily.
98342.m: With a blocked nose you snore more easily.

98343.q: In which position do many people snore most?
98343.e: Lying on your back, the tongue falls back a little. Then the throat gets narrow and you are more likely to snore.
98343.m: You snore most lying on your back.

98344.q: Which of these animals can also snore?
98344.e: Dogs also breathe through the nose and throat and can snore in their sleep, especially dogs with short noses.

98345.q: Who snores more often on average?
98345.e: Adult men snore more often than women and children.
98345.m: Men snore more often than women.

98346.e: The person snoring is asleep and usually does not hear it. The others in the room hear it all the better.
98346.m: It is usually the others who hear the snoring.

98347.q: Which little flap at the back of the mouth often flutters when you snore?
98347.e: The uvula hangs at the back of the roof of the mouth. When you snore, it can flutter together with the soft palate.
98347.m: The uvula hangs at the back of your mouth.

a: Something you do the same way every evening
98348.e: A bedtime routine is a fixed set of steps before sleeping, the same every evening. It helps you calm down.
98348.m: A bedtime routine is the same every evening.

98349.q: What is a good bedtime routine?
98349.e: A calm story is relaxing. Exciting films and wild games, on the other hand, wake you up.
98349.m: A bedtime story helps you fall asleep.

98350.q: What should you do every evening before going to sleep?
98350.e: Before sleeping you brush your teeth. That way they stay clean and healthy overnight.
98350.m: You brush your teeth before going to sleep.

98351.q: Why does a bedtime routine help?
a: The body notices that it is time to sleep
98351.e: If you do the same thing every evening, your body gets used to it. It then knows that it will soon be time to sleep.
98351.m: A fixed routine shows the body that it is time to sleep.

98352.q: What is a song that you sing to children to help them fall asleep called?
98352.e: A lullaby is a calm song for falling asleep. In the past it was sung while rocking the baby's cradle.
98352.m: You sing a lullaby to help someone fall asleep.

98353.q: Which animals do people often count when they cannot fall asleep?
98353.e: Counting sheep is an old tip. The steady counting is boring and is meant to make you tired.
98353.m: If you cannot fall asleep, you count sheep.

98354.q: Is it good to go to bed at about the same time every evening?
a: Yes, it helps you fall asleep
98354.e: Fixed bedtimes help your body clock. Then you get tired at the right time every evening.
98354.m: Fixed bedtimes help you fall asleep.

98355.q: Which drink suits an evening routine well?
98355.e: Warm milk contains no caffeine and is nicely warming. Drinks with caffeine, on the other hand, can keep you awake.
98355.m: In the evening it is better not to drink anything with caffeine.

98356.q: What do people often say to each other before going to sleep?
98356.e: With “Good night” you wish each other a good sleep. In many families it is part of the evening.
98356.m: Before going to sleep, people say “Good night”.

98357.q: Which cuddly toy is named after an American president?
98357.e: The teddy bear is named after President Theodore “Teddy” Roosevelt. It has been very popular for over 100 years.
98357.m: The teddy bear has a president's nickname.

98358.q: Why do many children have a cuddly toy in bed?
a: It comforts them and makes them feel safe
It wakes them in the morning
98358.e: A cuddly toy is familiar and soft. That gives a safe feeling at night.
98358.m: A cuddly toy gives a safe feeling.

98359.q: How can you clean a dirty cuddly toy?
98359.e: Many cuddly toys can be washed in the washing machine, best in a laundry bag. But you should check the label first.
98359.m: You can wash a dirty cuddly toy.

98360.q: What are most cuddly toys made of?
98360.e: Cuddly toys are made of soft fabric and filled with stuffing. That is why they are nice to squeeze.
98360.m: Cuddly toys are made of soft fabric.

98361.q: What is another name for a cuddly toy made of fluffy fabric?
98361.e: Plush is a soft fabric with short, fluffy hairs. That is why cuddly toys are often called plush toys.
98361.m: A fluffy cuddly toy is also called a plush toy.

98362.q: What is a small, soft cloth for babies, often with an animal's head, called?
98362.e: A comforter is soft and small. Babies like to hold it tight as they fall asleep.
98362.m: Babies like to cuddle a comforter.

98363.q: What do you do if your cuddly toy has a hole?
a: Put it out in the rain
98363.e: With a needle and thread you can sew up a hole in the fabric. Then no more stuffing falls out.
98363.m: You can sew up a hole in a cuddly toy.

98364.q: What kind of animal is Winnie the Pooh?
98364.e: Winnie the Pooh is a teddy bear from children's books. Eeyore the donkey and Tigger the tiger are his friends.
98364.m: Winnie the Pooh is a bear.

98365.q: What is a night light for?
a: It gives a little light in the dark
It wakes you in the morning
98365.e: A night light glows faintly at night. That way you can find your way in the dark.
98365.m: A night light glows faintly at night.

98366.q: Which light is better for sleep at night?
98366.e: Bright light wakes you up. A faint, warm light disturbs your sleep the least.
98366.m: At night, faint warm light is best.

98367.q: When does a night light with a sensor switch on?
98367.e: A light sensor notices when it gets dark. Then the night light comes on by itself.
98367.m: A night light with a sensor comes on in the dark.

98368.q: Why do many children like a night light?
a: They are less afraid of the dark
98368.e: Many children are scared in a completely dark room. A small light is calming.
98368.m: A night light takes away the fear of the dark.

98369.q: Which object in the sky is a natural night light?
98369.e: The moon is lit up by the sun and so it shines at night. At full moon it is quite bright outside.
98369.m: The moon is the night light in the sky.

98370.q: What does a night light without a cable need?
98370.e: Without a cable, a lamp needs a battery or a rechargeable battery. The power is stored in it.
98370.m: A night light without a cable needs a battery.

98371.q: In what kind of room does the body sleep best?
a: With a torch shining in your face
98371.e: Darkness tells the body that it is night. That is why you sleep most deeply in the dark.
98371.m: The body sleeps best in the dark.

98372.q: Where do you often plug in a small night light?
98372.e: Many night lights plug straight into the socket. That way they get power and glow.
98372.m: Many night lights plug into the socket.

98373.q: What often happens when you see someone yawn?
98373.e: Yawning is catching. Often it is enough just to see someone yawn or to read about it.

98374.q: When do we yawn especially often?
98374.e: In the evening and in the morning we are tired. Then we yawn especially often.
98374.m: If you are tired, you yawn often.

98375.q: What do we do with our mouth when we yawn?
98375.e: When we yawn, we open our mouth wide and breathe in deeply. Then we breathe out slowly.
98375.m: When you yawn, you open your mouth wide.

98376.e: Many animals with a backbone yawn, for example lions, cats and monkeys.

98377.q: Roughly how long does a yawn last?
98377.e: A yawn lasts about 6 seconds on average. So it is over quickly.
98377.m: A yawn only lasts a few seconds.

98378.q: What do you do out of politeness when you yawn?
a: Put your hand in front of your mouth
Sing loudly at the same time
98378.e: You hold your hand in front of your open mouth. That is considered polite.
98378.m: When you yawn, you put your hand in front of your mouth.

98379.q: Apart from tiredness, when else do we often yawn?
98379.e: Boredom also makes us yawn. Many people know this from long waits.

98380.q: What do people often do together with yawning when they wake up?
98380.e: After waking up, many people yawn and stretch their arms and legs. That wakes the muscles up.
98380.m: After waking up, you yawn and stretch.

98381.q: What is it called when someone gets up and walks around in their sleep?
98381.e: When sleepwalking, someone gets up in their sleep and walks around without really being awake.
98381.m: Someone who walks around in their sleep is sleepwalking.

98382.e: Sleepwalking happens much more often in children than in adults.

98383.q: Does a sleepwalker remember it in the morning?
98383.e: Sleepwalkers are not really awake. That is why they usually know nothing about it in the morning.
98383.m: Sleepwalkers usually do not remember it.

98384.q: What should you do with a sleepwalker?
a: Calmly lead them back to bed
98384.e: You gently lead a sleepwalker back to bed. You should not frighten them.
98384.m: You calmly lead a sleepwalker back to bed.

98385.q: What are the eyes often like during sleepwalking?
98385.e: Sleepwalkers often have their eyes open. Even so, they are asleep and staring into space.
98385.m: Sleepwalkers often have their eyes open.

98386.q: Does sleepwalking in children usually stop again?
98386.e: In most children, sleepwalking stops by itself by the teenage years.

98387.q: What protects a sleepwalker from accidents?
a: Stretching a rope across the room
98387.e: Safe stairs and windows prevent falls. Things lying around should be tidied away.
98387.m: Safe stairs and windows protect sleepwalkers.

98388.q: Is a sleepwalker awake while walking around?
98388.e: Sleepwalking happens in deep sleep, usually in the first half of the night. That is why the sleepwalker notices nothing.

98389.q: What can make sleepwalking happen more often?
98389.e: Lack of sleep can trigger sleepwalking. So getting enough sleep helps against it.

98390.q: Mia sleeps 10 hours every night. How many hours does she sleep in a week?
98390.e: A week has 7 nights. 7 times 10 hours makes 70 hours.

98391.q: How many hours of sleep do adults need each night?
98391.e: Adults are advised to get 7 to 9 hours of sleep a night.
98391.m: Adults need 7 to 9 hours of sleep.

98392.e: Newborn babies sleep about 14 to 17 hours a day, spread over lots of little naps.

98393.q: Roughly how much of their life do people spend asleep?
98393.e: If you sleep 8 out of 24 hours, you sleep a third of the day. So you spend about a third of your life asleep.
98393.m: We spend about a third of our lives asleep.

98394.q: Which animal sleeps up to 20 hours a day?
98394.e: Koalas eat eucalyptus leaves, which provide little energy. That is why they sleep and rest for up to 20 hours a day.
98394.m: The koala is a great sleeper.

98395.q: Tim gets up at 7 o'clock and wants to sleep for 10 hours. When does he need to go to bed?
98395.e: From 9 pm to 7 am is 10 hours. You work out 7 o'clock minus 10 hours.
98395.m: If you get up early, you need to go to bed early.

98396.q: Lea sleeps from 8 pm to 7 am. How many hours is that?
98396.e: From 8 pm to midnight is 4 hours, from midnight to 7 am is 7 hours. 4 plus 7 makes 11 hours.
98396.m: You add up the hours of sleep across midnight.

98397.q: How many hours of sleep do teenagers aged 13 to 18 need?
98397.e: Teenagers need about 8 to 10 hours of sleep, a bit more than adults.
98397.m: Teenagers need 8 to 10 hours of sleep.

98398.q: What are the clothes you put on to sleep called?
98398.e: Pyjamas are comfortable clothes for the night. You put them on before going to sleep.

98399.q: In which country do pyjamas have their origin?
98399.e: Pyjamas originally come from India and its neighbouring countries. The British brought them to Europe.

98400.q: Which two parts do pyjamas usually have?
98400.e: Pyjamas usually have a top and long or short trousers.
98400.m: Pyjamas have a top and trousers.

98401.q: What is a long shirt for sleeping in without trousers called?
98401.e: A nightdress is a long, loose shirt for the night. No trousers go with it.
98401.m: A nightdress is a long shirt for sleeping.

98402.q: Which fabric is popular for pyjamas because it is soft and soaks up sweat?
98402.e: Cotton is soft, feels pleasant on the skin and soaks up sweat well.
98402.m: Cotton pyjamas are soft and comfortable.

98403.q: Why do you put on pyjamas to sleep?
98403.e: Pyjamas are loose and soft. And you do not bring the dirt from the day into bed.

98405.q: What do you wear with your pyjamas in winter against cold feet?
98405.e: Warm socks keep your feet warm. With warm feet, you fall asleep more easily.
98405.m: Warm socks help against cold feet in bed.

98406.q: Which colour of light from screens disturbs sleep most?
98406.e: Screens give off a lot of blue light. It tells the body that it is still daytime and keeps you awake.
98406.m: Blue screen light keeps you awake.

98407.q: When is it best to put screens away before going to sleep?
98407.e: Experts advise putting screens away about an hour before going to sleep. That way the body can wind down.
98407.m: Put screens away about an hour before going to sleep.

98408.q: Where is the best place for your phone at night?
a: In bed next to your head
98408.e: In the bedroom, messages and light from the phone can disturb your sleep. That is why it is better left outside.
98408.m: Your phone sleeps better outside the bedroom.

98409.q: What is better than a screen before falling asleep?
98409.e: A book does not glow and does not get you excited. Reading calms you before sleep.
98409.m: Before sleeping, it is better to read a book.

98410.q: What often happens to your eyes after a lot of screen time?
98410.e: When you look at a screen, you blink less. That is why your eyes get tired and dry.
98410.m: A lot of screen time makes your eyes tired.

98411.q: What helps you keep track of your screen time?
98411.e: With a timer or alarm clock you know when your time is up.
98411.m: A timer helps you stick to your screen time.

98412.q: What is better for the body than hours in front of a screen?
98412.e: Moving in the fresh air strengthens muscles and bones. In the evening you are then pleasantly tired.
98412.m: Playing outside is good for the body.

98413.q: What does an exciting screen game in the evening do to the brain?
98413.e: Exciting games stimulate the brain. Afterwards it takes longer to fall asleep.
98413.m: Exciting games in the evening keep the brain awake.

99009.q: Which flower is often called the “queen of flowers”?
99009.e: The rose has been one of the most popular flowers for a very long time. That is why it is often called the queen of flowers.
99009.m: The rose is known as the queen of flowers.

99010.q: When are garden roses usually cut back hard?
99010.e: In spring, when no more hard frost is coming, old and dead shoots are cut off. Afterwards strong new shoots with flowers grow.
99010.m: Roses are cut back in spring.

99011.q: What colour is the rose given as a sign of love?
99011.e: A red rose has long been a sign of love. People give it on Valentine's Day, for example.
99011.m: The red rose is a sign of love.

99012.q: What are many roses known for when you sniff them?
99012.e: Many roses smell sweet and delicate. Their petals are even used to make scented oil.

99013.q: Which fruit belongs to the same plant family as the rose?
99013.e: The rose and the apple both belong to the rose family. Cherries and strawberries are in it too.
99013.m: The apple is related to the rose.

99014.q: How many petals does a simple wild rose usually have?
99014.e: Wild roses such as the dog rose usually have five petals. Garden roses often have many more.
99014.m: A wild rose usually has five petals.

99015.q: What do you cut off roses in summer so that new flowers come?
99015.e: If you cut off faded flowers, the rose puts its strength into new flowers. That way it flowers for longer.
99015.m: Faded rose flowers are cut off.

99016.q: What does a rose in the garden especially need to flower well?
99016.e: Roses love a sunny spot. In the shade they flower much less.

99017.q: What is a rose that grows up walls and arches called?
99017.e: Climbing roses have long shoots. They are tied to trellises, arches or house walls.
99017.m: A climbing rose grows up walls.

99018.q: What do many people call the pelargonium in the window box?
99018.e: The popular balcony flower is really called a pelargonium. But in everyday life most people say geranium.
99018.m: The balcony geranium is really a pelargonium.

99019.q: What are the wild relatives of the geranium that also grow in Swiss meadows called?
99019.e: Geraniums and cranesbills belong to the same plant family. Their fruits look like a long bird's beak.
99019.m: The cranesbill is a wild relative of the geranium.

99020.q: Which continent do most geraniums come from?
99020.e: Most balcony geraniums originally come from southern Africa. It is warm and sunny there.

99021.q: What can geraniums not cope with at all?
99021.e: Geraniums die in frost. That is why they are brought indoors in autumn.
99021.m: Geraniums must be protected from frost.

99022.q: What do geraniums in pots not like at all?
99022.e: Geraniums need regular watering. But if water is left standing in the pot, their roots rot.
99022.m: Geraniums don't like standing water in the pot.

99023.q: What colour are geraniums in Switzerland very often?
99023.e: There are geraniums in red, pink, white and purple. The best known are the red geraniums.
99023.m: Many geraniums have bright red flowers.

99024.q: What happens with some geraniums when you rub their leaves?
99024.e: With scented geraniums, the leaves smell of lemon or rose, for example, when rubbed. That is why they are called that.
99024.m: Scented geraniums smell when you rub their leaves.

99025.q: Which spot do geraniums like best?
99025.e: Geraniums come from a warm, sunny country. They flower most beautifully in the sun.

99026.q: In which season do sunflowers bloom?
99026.e: Sunflowers bloom in summer, when it is warm and sunny. In autumn the seeds then ripen.

99027.q: What does the stem of a sunflower feel like?
99027.e: The stem and leaves of the sunflower are covered in small, stiff hairs. That is why they feel rough.
99027.m: The sunflower's stem is rough and hairy.

99028.q: In what pattern do the seeds sit in a sunflower?
99028.e: The seeds are arranged in many spirals running to the left and to the right. That way a great many seeds fit on the flower head.
99028.m: The sunflower's seeds sit in spirals.

99029.q: Which insects like to collect nectar from sunflowers?
99029.e: The sunflower's many small flowers offer nectar and pollen. That is why bees and bumblebees like to visit them.

99030.q: Which continent does the sunflower come from?
99030.e: The sunflower first grew in North America. Sailors brought it to Europe a long time ago.
99030.m: The sunflower comes from North America.

99031.q: Which animals like eating sunflower seeds at the bird table in winter?
99031.e: Tits and other birds like pecking at sunflower seeds. The seeds give them a lot of energy.

99032.q: How tall can a sunflower in the garden grow?
a: Only as tall as a shoe
99032.e: Many sunflowers grow two to three metres tall. That makes them taller than adults.
99032.m: Sunflowers can grow taller than a person.

99033.q: What does a sunflower need to grow well?
99033.e: As its name says, the sunflower loves the sun. In a bright, warm spot it grows big and strong.

99034.q: What is the big brown centre of the sunflower really?
99034.e: The centre is made of a great many tiny flowers. Each little flower later becomes a seed.
99034.m: The centre of the sunflower is made of many small flowers.

99035.q: Which country does the dahlia come from?
99035.e: Dahlias grow wild in Mexico. There the dahlia is even the national flower.

99036.q: What do dahlias grow from again each year?
99036.e: Dahlias form thick tubers in the ground. New shoots grow from them in spring.

99037.q: How big can the flowers of some dahlias get?
99037.e: There are very large dahlia varieties. Their flowers can get as wide as a plate.
99037.m: Some dahlias have flowers as big as a plate.

99039.e: Dahlias bloom from summer until the first frost. That way they bring colour to the garden in autumn too.
99039.m: Dahlias bloom from summer into autumn.

99040.q: Which flower colour do dahlias not come in?
99040.e: Dahlias come in almost every colour. But there is no truly blue dahlia.
99040.m: There are no truly blue dahlias.

99041.q: What do pompon dahlias look like?
99041.e: Pompon dahlias have lots of rolled-up petals. That is why their flowers are round like little balls.
99041.m: Pompon dahlias are round like balls.

99042.q: Which animals like to nibble young dahlias in spring?
99042.e: Slugs and snails love the tender young shoots of dahlias. That is why gardeners protect the plants well.
99042.m: Slugs and snails like eating young dahlias.

99044.q: What colours are marigold flowers usually?
99044.e: Marigolds glow a strong yellow and orange. Some also have reddish brown spots.
99044.m: Marigolds have yellow and orange flowers.

99045.q: What do the leaves of marigolds smell like?
99045.e: Marigolds have a strong, spicy smell. Some people like it, others don't.

99046.q: Why do gardeners like to plant marigolds between vegetables?
a: To make the vegetables grow faster
99046.e: The roots of marigolds drive away tiny worms in the soil. This keeps the vegetables healthier.
99046.m: Marigolds protect vegetables from pests in the soil.

99047.q: Which country do many marigolds come from?
99047.e: Marigolds originally come from Mexico and Central America. There they are used to decorate big festivals.

99048.q: How long does a marigold in the garden usually live?
99048.e: Most marigolds are annuals. They are sown again every spring.
99048.m: Marigolds are sown again every year.

99049.q: Which creatures especially like eating marigolds?
99049.e: Slugs and snails love marigolds. That is why marigolds can lure them away from other plants.
99049.m: Slugs and snails love eating marigolds.

99050.q: Until when do marigolds bloom in the garden?
99050.e: Marigolds bloom all summer. Only the first frost in autumn ends their flowering.
99050.m: Marigolds bloom until the first frost.

99051.q: When are pansies often planted on the balcony?
99051.e: Pansies cope well with cold. That is why they bloom in early spring, when other flowers are still asleep.

99052.q: What do the markings on many pansy flowers look like?
99052.e: The dark patches in the middle look like a little face. That is why children especially like this flower.
99052.m: Pansies often have a little face.

99053.q: Roughly how tall do pansies grow?
99053.e: Pansies stay small and grow only about 10 to 20 centimetres tall. That is why they fit well in bowls and boxes.

99054.q: What can you do with pansy flowers in the kitchen?
99054.e: Pansy flowers are edible. You can put them on a salad or a cake, for example.

99055.q: How many petals does a pansy have?
99055.e: A pansy has five petals. The bottom petal is the biggest.

99056.q: Which group of plants does the pansy belong to?
99056.e: The pansy is a kind of violet. Its scientific name begins with Viola, the name of the violets.
99056.m: The pansy belongs to the violets.

99057.e: There are pansies in yellow, blue, purple, white, orange and many mixtures. Often there are several colours on one flower.

99058.q: Where does the wild pansy grow?
99058.e: The wild pansy grows in meadows and fields. Its flowers are smaller than those of the garden kind.
99058.m: The wild pansy grows in meadows.

99059.q: What do hydrangea flowers often look like?
99059.e: Many hydrangeas have big, round flower heads. They are made of many small flowers.
99059.m: Hydrangeas often have round balls of flowers.

99060.q: What does a hydrangea need especially a lot of?
99060.e: Hydrangeas drink a lot. Their scientific name even means something like water vessel.
99060.m: Hydrangeas need a lot of water.

99061.q: What decides whether some hydrangeas flower blue or pink?
99061.e: In acidic soil with aluminium, some hydrangeas flower blue. In chalky soil they turn pink.
99061.m: The soil decides whether some hydrangeas turn blue or pink.

99062.q: Which spot do hydrangeas like best?
99062.e: In blazing sun hydrangeas quickly go limp. They like partial shade best.

99063.q: Which country does the garden hydrangea come from?
99063.e: The popular garden hydrangea comes from Japan. From there it came to Europe.
99063.m: The garden hydrangea comes from Japan.

99064.q: What often happens to hydrangea flowers in autumn?
99064.e: The flower balls dry on the bush and change colour. You can cut them for lovely dried bouquets.
99064.m: Dried hydrangea flowers are good for dried bouquets.

99065.q: Is a hydrangea a tree, a shrub or a grass?
99065.e: Hydrangeas grow as shrubs with several woody shoots. They usually grow about one to two metres tall.

99066.q: What do drooping, limp leaves on a hydrangea usually show?
99066.e: When the soil is too dry, hydrangeas let their leaves and flowers droop. After watering they often recover quickly.

99067.e: Hydrangeas bloom from early summer to late summer. Many flowers last a very long time.

99068.q: What does a lily grow from?
99068.e: Lilies form a bulb made of scales in the ground. A new stem grows from it every year.

99069.q: For which pet are lilies very poisonous?
99069.e: Even a little pollen or a few lily leaves can make cats seriously ill. Cat owners should not have lilies in the home.
99069.m: Lilies are very poisonous for cats.

99070.q: What do many lilies in a bunch of flowers smell like?
99070.e: Many lilies have a very strong, sweet scent. Some people even find it too strong in a room.
99070.m: Many lilies smell strong and sweet.

99071.e: The lily beetle is a bright red beetle. It and its larvae eat holes in lily leaves.
99071.m: The lily beetle is a red beetle that eats lily leaves.

99072.q: How many petals does a lily flower have?
99072.e: A lily has six petals. They often form a trumpet or a star.

99073.q: What colour is the Madonna lily?
99073.e: The Madonna lily has big white flowers. It is a very old garden plant.

99074.q: What can lily pollen do to clothes?
99074.e: Lily pollen is orange brown and stains strongly. That is why it is often picked off cut flowers.

99075.q: Which orange lily grows in sunny meadows in the Alps?
99075.e: The fire lily has bright orange flowers. In the Alps it likes to grow on sunny slopes.
99075.m: The fire lily glows orange in the Alps.

99076.q: Around which festival does the peony often bloom?
99076.e: The peony blooms in May and June. That is roughly the time of Whitsun, which is where its German name, Pfingstrose (Whitsun rose), comes from.

99077.q: In German the peony is called a “Whitsun rose”. Is it a real rose?
99077.e: The peony looks similar but belongs to a plant family of its own. It also has no thorns.
99077.m: The peony is not a real rose.

99078.q: Which small creatures often crawl on peony buds?
99078.e: The buds give off a sweet juice. The ants like it, and they do not harm the plant.

99079.q: What do peony flowers look like?
99079.e: Peonies have big, lush flowers. Many are double and round like a ball.

99080.q: How long can a peony grow in the same spot?
99080.e: A peony can live to a great age. In the same spot it often flowers for decades.
99080.m: Peonies can live for a very long time.

99081.q: What does a peony not like at all?
99081.e: Peonies do not like being moved. After transplanting they often do not flower for several years.
99081.m: It is better not to move peonies.

99082.e: Peonies flower in many shades from white through pink to dark red. There are also yellow varieties.
99082.m: Peonies often flower pink, red or white.

99083.q: What happens to the stems of a garden peony in autumn?
99083.e: In most garden peonies the stems wilt in autumn. In spring the plant grows again from the root.
99083.m: The peony grows again from the root every spring.

99084.q: Which small creatures often sit in crowds on nasturtiums?
99084.e: Black aphids love nasturtiums. That is why they are sometimes planted to lure aphids away from other plants.

99085.e: Nasturtium tastes slightly hot, similar to cress or pepper. This comes from a substance in the plant.

99086.e: The leaves are round and the stalk is attached in the middle. They look like little plates or umbrellas.
99086.m: Nasturtium has round leaves like little plates.

99087.q: What happens to drops of water on a nasturtium leaf?
a: They vanish into the leaf at once
99087.e: The leaves are water-repellent. The drops roll off like pearls and take dirt with them.

99088.q: What colours are nasturtium flowers often?
99088.e: The flowers glow in warm colours such as orange, yellow and red. They attract many insects.
99088.m: Nasturtiums flower orange, yellow or red.

99089.q: Which continent does the nasturtium come from?
99089.e: The nasturtium originally comes from the Andes in South America. Today it grows in many gardens.
99089.m: The nasturtium comes from South America.

99091.q: How does nasturtium often grow in the garden?
99091.e: Nasturtium forms long shoots. It creeps over the ground or climbs up fences.

99092.q: Where can you plant nasturtiums well if you have no garden?
99092.e: Nasturtium needs light and grows well in pots and boxes. The shoots then hang down nicely.
99092.m: Nasturtium grows well in a window box.

99093.q: What does the centre of a coneflower look like?
99093.e: The centre of the flower bulges upwards. That is why it reminds people of a little hat; in German the plant is called “sun hat”.
99093.m: The coneflower has a domed centre like a hat.

99094.q: What colour are the flowers of the purple coneflower?
99094.e: The purple coneflower flowers pink to purplish red. Its centre is orange brown.
99094.m: The purple coneflower flowers pink to purple.

99095.q: What colour is the yellow coneflower?
99095.e: In the yellow coneflower the petals are golden yellow. The centre is almost black.
99095.m: The yellow coneflower has a dark centre.

99096.q: Which continent does the coneflower come from?
99096.e: The coneflower grows wild in meadows in North America. Today it grows in many Swiss gardens.
99096.m: The coneflower comes from North America.

99097.q: Which creatures especially like visiting the coneflower?
99097.e: The coneflower has lots of nectar and pollen. That is why bees, bumblebees and butterflies like flying to it.
99097.m: Bees and butterflies love the coneflower.

99098.q: What is the purple coneflower also used for?
99098.e: Drops and tea are made from the purple coneflower, also called echinacea. They are used for colds, for example.
99098.m: The purple coneflower is a medicinal plant.

99099.q: Does the coneflower come back every year?
99099.e: The coneflower is a perennial. In winter it rests in the ground and sprouts again in spring.
99099.m: The coneflower comes back every year.

99100.q: Which spot does the coneflower like best?
99100.e: The coneflower loves the sun. In a bright spot it flowers abundantly.

99101.q: What colour are forget-me-not flowers usually?
99101.e: Forget-me-nots have small sky-blue flowers. They grow in little clusters.
99101.m: The forget-me-not usually flowers light blue.

99102.q: What colour is the small centre of a forget-me-not flower?
99102.e: In the middle of each blue flower there is a small yellow ring. It shows insects the way to the nectar.
99102.m: The forget-me-not has a yellow centre.

99103.e: The flowers are only a few millimetres across. But there are a great many at once.
99103.m: The forget-me-not has very small flowers.

99104.q: When does the forget-me-not bloom in the garden?
99104.e: The forget-me-not blooms in spring, often together with tulips. After that it fades.

99105.q: How many petals does a forget-me-not flower have?
99105.e: Each small flower has five petals. They are arranged around the yellow centre.

99106.q: What colour are forget-me-not buds often before they turn blue?
99106.e: The buds are often pink. When they open, the flowers turn blue.

99107.q: Where does the water forget-me-not grow?
99107.e: The water forget-me-not loves wet ground. You find it by streams, ponds and in marshes.
99107.m: The water forget-me-not grows by water.

99108.e: The name says: don't forget me. That is why the flower is given as a sign of remembrance.
99108.m: The forget-me-not is a sign of remembrance.

99195.q: Which finger do people especially often forget when washing their hands?
99195.e: The thumb sticks out a little and is often missed when rubbing. You should hold it with your other hand and wash it separately.
99195.m: When washing your hands, remember your thumbs.

99196.q: When must you always wash your hands?
99196.e: Before eating, you wash germs away so they do not get into your mouth with the food.
99196.m: You always wash your hands before eating.

99197.q: Why do you wash your hands after stroking a pet?
a: There can be germs on the fur
So the animal does not get cold
99197.e: Animals have germs in their fur and around their mouth that can make people ill. Washing your hands removes them.
99197.m: After stroking animals, you wash your hands.

99198.q: What do you do first when washing your hands?
99198.e: First you wet your hands, then you soap them. After that you rinse and dry them.
99198.m: When washing your hands, you wet them first.

99199.q: Why do you wash your hands after playing outside?
a: To make your hands smell nice
99199.e: Outside, your hands come into contact with soil and lots of germs. You wash them off with water and soap.
99199.m: Washing your hands removes dirt and germs.

99200.q: What do you do after washing your hands?
a: Rub your hands on your trousers
Put your hands in the soil
99200.e: Germs stick more easily to wet hands. That is why you dry them well with a clean towel after washing.
99200.m: After washing, you dry your hands well.

99201.q: Which doctor realised as early as about 1847 that hand washing protects patients?
99201.e: Ignaz Semmelweis had the doctors in his hospital clean their hands thoroughly. After that, far fewer patients became ill.
99201.m: Ignaz Semmelweis showed that clean hands save lives.

99202.q: What helps children wash their hands for long enough?
99202.e: Singing a short song like “Happy Birthday” twice takes about 20 seconds. That way you know when you are done.
99202.m: A song helps you wash your hands for long enough.

99203.q: What cleans your hands when you are out and there is no water?
99203.e: Hand sanitiser kills many germs. But if dirt is visible, washing with water and soap is better.

99204.q: What does soap do to dirt and grease?
99204.e: Soap loosens grease and dirt from the skin. Then you can rinse everything away with water.

99205.q: What has soap been made from for a long time?
99205.e: If you boil fat or oil with lye, soap is formed. People have made soap this way for thousands of years.
99205.m: Soap is made from fat and lye.

99206.q: What do you get when you rub soap with water?
99206.e: Soap and water together make lots of tiny bubbles. This foam helps with cleaning.

99207.q: What is the name of a simple, hard soap without perfume that people also used to wash clothes with in the past?
99207.e: Plain household soap is a simple, hard soap without perfume. In the past, people used it to wash their hands, bodies and clothes.
99207.m: Plain household soap is a simple, hard soap.

99208.q: What do you call soap that comes in a bottle with a pump?
99208.e: Liquid soap is runny and comes out of a dispenser. You just press the pump.
99208.m: Liquid soap comes from a pump dispenser.

99209.q: What happens to a bar of soap if you use it often?
99209.e: Every time you wash, a little soap dissolves in the water. That is why the bar gets smaller and smaller over time.
99209.m: Soap gets smaller as you use it.

99210.q: Where should a bar of soap be put after you use it?
a: In a soap dish to dry
99210.e: In a soap dish, the soap can drip and dry. If it lies in water, it becomes soft and slimy.
99210.m: Soap should be able to dry after washing.

99211.e: A full bathtub needs a lot of water. A short shower usually needs much less.

99212.q: Why do people shower after sport?
99212.e: You sweat when you do sport. Showering washes the sweat off, otherwise your skin soon starts to smell.
99212.m: After sport, you wash off the sweat in the shower.

99213.q: What can you turn off while you soap yourself in the shower?
99213.e: You do not need water while you are soaping yourself. If you turn it off for a moment, you save a lot of water.
99213.m: You can turn the water off while soaping yourself.

99214.q: Why do many showers have a rubber mat?
99214.e: Wet tiles are very slippery. A mat with little bumps helps you stand safely.
99214.m: A shower mat stops you from slipping.
